proposed.statement: For every declared pair \((m,\mathsf J_{-})\) for which \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\ne\varnothing\), characterize \(R_n(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}))\) by matching same-class upper and lower bounds, construct a bandwidth rule using neither declared object, and derive a necessary-and-sufficient uniform-consistency criterion for triangular or union classes. The characterization must recover the isolated and pervasive polynomial rates and vanishing risk for every fixed positive exponential modulus represented by a nonempty named class.
proposed.justification: This is the genuine open content: arbitrary irregular mass requires an explicit global upper map and legal multiplicity-aware lower families within one named class.
proposed.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate covers pointwise regular and severe variation, Gaiffas2007SharpSupNorm covers spatial sup-norm normalization under positive continuous univariate density, and Gaiffas2009Uniform and AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 cover univariate designs with finitely many zeros under different losses; none gives an arbitrary-modulus two-sided boundary-uniform characterization indexed by a lower-mass modulus and lower thin-site packing declaration.
proposed.consumer: A solved criterion would tell \(\texttt{rd2d}\) whether an observed pattern of side counts permits a uniformly consistent curve before fitting or reporting it.

payload.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and \(m(r)>0\) for every \(0<r\le h_0\). For every nonempty class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\), let \(\overline\tau_n(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\widehat\tau_n(x)\}\), where \(\Pi_I\) is Euclidean projection onto the interval \(I\). There are constants \(A,C,c,a>0\), depending only on the fixed envelopes, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\min\left[ L,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\\nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)}}
 \left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}\right],
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). The estimator in this display uses neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\); they occur only in its guarantee. Conversely, if \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\), then
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh
\]
whenever either \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), or \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\). Hence a sufficient uniform-consistency condition for a sequence of nonempty such classes with lower moduli \(m_n\) is the existence of \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\); a necessary condition is that the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible values of \(h\) in the preceding display tends to zero. With polynomial profiles, the lower display yields the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp1\) and the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp h^{-1}\); together with \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), these rates are exact. payload.proof_tex:
For a law \(P\) in the revised class, define the finite one-sided score measure
\[
 \mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t).
\]
If \(x\in\mathcal B\) and \(r>0\), set \(s=\min\{h_0,r/2\}\). Positivity of \(m\) and \(\mathrm{ass:declared\text{-}modulus\text{-}lower\text{-}mass}\), which is a member property of \(\mathrm{def:modulus\text{-}profile\text{-}class}\), give
\[
 \mu_{t,P}\{z:d(z,x)<r\}\ge q_{t,P}(x,s)\ge m(s)>0. \tag{40}
\]
Thus \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) on both sides. The unique Lipschitz representative and the definition of its trace consequently give
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x). \tag{41}
\]
Under \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), sharp assignment makes \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\) equivalent to \(T_i=t\). Therefore the conditional mean of each observed side average is the corresponding average of \(g_{t,P}(X_i)\). The bounded-trace member property yields \(\tau_P(x)\in[-2L,2L]\); projection onto this closed interval cannot increase pointwise distance to \(\tau_P(x)\), and the clipped loss is at most \(4L\).

We prove the upper display. Fix \(h\) with \(h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\) and \(nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)\). Let \(z_1,\ldots,z_K\) be a maximal \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\). It is an \(h\)-net, and \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) gives \(K\le C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}\). For each \(j,t\), \(N_{t,n}(z_j,h)\) is binomial with success probability \(q_{t,P}(z_j,h)\ge m(h)\), by independent sampling and the class's lower-mass property. If \(N\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), then Markov's inequality applied to \(2^{-N}\) gives
\[
 \Pr\{N\le nq/2\}
 \le 2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n
 \le \exp(-nq/8), \tag{42}
\]
where the last inequality follows from \(1-y\le e^{-y}\) and \((\log2)/2-1/2<-1/8\). Hence a union bound, monotonicity in the threshold, and \(q\ge m(h)\) show
\[
 \Pr_P(H_h^c)\le 2C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}, \tag{43}
\]
where \(H_h\) is the event on which all \(N_{t,n}(z_j,h)\ge nm(h)/2\). For every \(x\in\mathcal B\), select a net point \(z_j\) with \(d(x,z_j)\le h\). The inclusion \(B(z_j,h)\subseteq B(x,2h)\) implies on \(H_h\) that
\[
 \inf_{x\in\mathcal B,\,t\in\{0,1\}}N_{t,n}(x,2h)\ge nm(h)/2. \tag{44}
\]
Choose the constant \(A\) so that the right-hand side of (44) is at least \(8\log(e+n/(2h))\). Then \(2h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\) for every \(x,t\) on \(H_h\).

Condition on the scores. For any selected nonempty averaging set at \((x,b,t)\), Lipschitz smoothness and (41) give
\[
 \left|\frac1{N_{t,n}(x,b)}\sum_{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le b}g_{t,P}(X_i)-\theta_{t,P}(x)\right|\le Lb. \tag{45}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\), simultaneously over every candidate disk pattern, the conditional expected normalized Gaussian error is at most
\[
 \sqrt{2\log\!\left(4|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\right)}+1\le C\sqrt{\log(e+n)}. \tag{46}
\]
Because every \(b\in\mathcal H_n\) satisfies \(b\le h_0<1\), \(\log(e+n)\le C\log(e+n/b)\). Combining (45)--(46) with the minimizing property in \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\), and comparing the selected criterion to the admissible candidate \(2h\), gives on \(H_h\)
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 \le C\left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}. \tag{47}
\]
Here both side errors have been added, and (44) was used in the stochastic term. Projection leaves the error no larger. On \(H_h^c\), the clipped error is at most \(4L\). Equations (43) and (47) therefore yield
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}
   +CLh^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}. \tag{48}
\]
Increasing \(A\), if necessary, makes the last term at most \(CLh\), since \(e^{-nm(h)/8}\le(e+n/h)^{-A/8}\). The deterministic clipped bound supplies the first argument \(L\) of the minimum when no scale qualifies. Taking the infimum over qualifying dyadic pairs proves the upper bracket. The sample map in \(\mathrm{def:mass\text{-}adaptive\text{-}estimator}\) and the projection use neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\).

We next prove the lower display within the same class. Choose any member \(P^\circ\) of the assumed nonempty class and retain its score marginal and assignment geometry. On an extension carrying independent standard normal variables \(Z_0,Z_1\), define a baseline law \(P_0\) by \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\). The score-dependent class properties are unchanged, while the side regressions and traces are zero, so the response smoothness, boundedness, Gaussian-error, sharp-assignment, and consistency properties all hold. Thus \(P_0\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\).

Let \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\ge1\). The class's lower-profile property and the definition of \(\mathsf J_P\) supply \(h\)-separated points \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) for which \(a_{P_0}(x_j,h)\le u\). Choose \(t_j\) attaining this minimum and put
\[
 \eta_h=\frac{Lh}{12},\qquad
 \psi_{j,h}(z)=\left(1-\frac{3d(z,x_j)}h\right)_+.
\]
Define \(P_j\) by retaining the baseline score law and errors and shifting only the potential outcome on side \(t_j\): add \(\eta_h\psi_{j,h}(X)\) when \(t_j=1\), and subtract it when \(t_j=0\). The added regression is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz because \(\psi_{j,h}\) is \(3/h\)-Lipschitz; its absolute trace is at most \(Lh/12<L\), since \(h\le h_0<1\). All design properties remain unchanged, and the error around the shifted conditional mean is still \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\). Hence every \(P_j\) belongs to \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\).

By (40)--(41), each center is in both one-sided supports and the target shift at \(x_j\) equals \(\eta_h\). If \(k\ne j\), then \(d(x_j,x_k)\ge h\), so \(\psi_{k,h}(x_j)=0\). Consequently
\[
 \|\tau_{P_j}-\tau_{P_k}\|_\infty\ge\eta_h,
 \qquad 0\le j<k\le M. \tag{49}
\]
Conditionally on a score value on the perturbed assignment side, the observed outcome changes from a normal mean zero to a normal mean \(s_j\eta_h\psi_{j,h}(X)\), with \(s_j\in\{-1,1\}\), and it does not change elsewhere. Direct integration of the Gaussian log-likelihood ratio gives conditional relative entropy \(\eta_h^2\psi_{j,h}(X)^2/(2\sigma^2)\). Since the tent is supported inside \(B(x_j,h/3)\subseteq B(x_j,h)\),
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 =\frac{n\eta_h^2}{2\sigma^2}\int\psi_{j,h}(z)^2\,d\mu_{t_j,P_0}(z)
 \le \frac{nL^2h^2u}{288\sigma^2}. \tag{50}
\]
If the first information condition holds, retain any one alternative and apply the two-law clause of \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), decreasing the numerical \(a\) so that (50) is at most \(1/8\). If \(M\ge2\) and the logarithmic condition holds, choose \(a\) so small that (50) is at most the multiple-law threshold times \(\log M\); this is possible uniformly over \(M\ge2\) because \(\log(M+1)/\log M\le\log3/\log2\). Applying the same lemma with the sup metric and \(2\delta=\eta_h\) proves \(R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh\).

For a sequence of nonempty classes, suppose \(h_n\downarrow0\), \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), and
\[
 \frac{nm_n(h_n)}{\log(e+n/h_n)}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{51}
\]
Then the eligibility condition holds eventually, \(Lh_n\to0\), and the square-root term in (48) tends to zero. This proves sufficient uniform consistency. Conversely, if the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible radii does not tend to zero, then along a subsequence one may choose feasible radii bounded below by a fixed positive constant (or half that constant when the supremum is not attained). The lower display then keeps the minimax risk bounded below by a positive constant, proving the stated necessary condition.

For \(m_\alpha\), \(\mathrm{prop:exponential\text{-}horn\text{-}consistency}\) supplies positivity and
\(m_\alpha(h)\asymp h^{\alpha+1}e^{-h^{-\alpha}}\). Set \(s_n=\{(\log n)/2\}^{-1/\alpha}\). Then
\[
 \frac{nm_\alpha(s_n)}{\log(e+n/s_n)}
 \asymp
 \frac{n^{1/2}s_n^{\alpha+1}}{\log n}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{52}
\]
Round \(s_n\) upward to the next point \(h_n\) of the dyadic grid. Eventually \(s_n\le h_n<2s_n\), both \(h_n\) and \(2h_n\) belong to \(\mathcal H_n\), and monotonicity of \(m_\alpha\) preserves (52). Thus the sufficient condition holds for the fixed exponential horn.

For polynomial profiles, set \(u=C_mh^\kappa\). If \(M\asymp1\), (50) is bounded at \(h\asymp n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\). If \(M\asymp h^{-1}\), the logarithmic information condition is met at \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), because \(nh^{\kappa+2}\asymp\log(1/h)\). The matching achievability bounds in \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\) make both rates exact.

Finally, the two generic displays can differ because the declared lower packing profile may be slack while the upper proof covers the entire boundary. On the circular pervasive witness, take \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=0\) for \(u<C_mh^\kappa\) and \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=1\) for \(u\ge C_mh^\kappa\). By \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), after choosing its fixed constants this defines a nonempty class containing the pervasive witness. Its declared lower profile exposes only \(M=1\), whereas (48) uses the global boundary entropy and therefore carries the global logarithm. This legal declaration certifies the stated possible gap and completes the two-sided bracket.
payload.justification: This theorem gives an explicit count-based global upper map and a legal same-class Lipschitz-tent converse indexed by the declared lower packing profile.
payload.gap: The two sides match in the isolated and pervasive polynomial regimes. For arbitrary declarations they can differ because \(\mathsf J_{-}\) may be slack while the upper argument covers the full boundary using global entropy.
payload.consumer: The \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflow can check the sufficient count condition before fitting and report a lower testing experiment when uniform consistency is impossible.

By (40)--(41), each center is in both one-sided supports and the target shift at \(x_j\) equals \(\eta_h\). If \(k\ne j\), then \(d(x_j,x_k)\ge h\), so \(\psi_{k,h}(x_j)=0\). Consequently
\[
 \|\tau_{P_j}-\tau_{P_k}\|_\infty\ge\eta_h,
 \qquad 0\le j<k\le M. \tag{49}
\]
Conditionally on a score value on the perturbed assignment side, the observed outcome changes from a normal mean zero to a normal mean \(s_j\eta_h\psi_{j,h}(X)\), with \(s_j\in\{-1,1\}\), and it does not change elsewhere. \[

 =\frac{n\eta_h^2}{2\sigma^2}\int\psi_{j,h}(z)^2\,d\mu_{t_j,P_0}(z)
 \le \frac{nL^2h^2u}{288\sigma^2}. \tag{50}
\]

For a sequence of nonempty classes, suppose \(h_n\downarrow0\), \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), and

\]

\(m_\alpha(h)\asymp h^{\alpha+1}e^{-h^{-\alpha}}\). Set \(s_n=\{(\log n)/2\}^{-1/\alpha}\). Then

 \asymp

\]

payload.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},\qquad
 t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), adopt the convention that the maximum below is zero when \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\). For almost every score vector, conditionally on the scores and with \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), one has for every \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
The conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most
\[
 \sqrt{2\log\{2(1\vee|\mathscr S_n|)\}}+1.
\]
payload.proof_tex:
Fix the scores. For a disk with center \(c\in\mathbb R^2\) and radius \(r\), membership of \(X_i\) is equivalent to
\[
 2c^{\mathsf T}X_i+s\ge\lVert X_i\rVert_2^2,\qquad
 s=r^2-\lVert c\rVert_2^2. \tag{17}
\]
Thus every disk trace is a sign pattern induced by \(n\) affine planes in the three-dimensional parameter \((c_1,c_2,s)\). A trace realized by a closed disk can be made strict by increasing its radius by less than the positive minimum distance to the finitely many excluded points, so equality in (17) creates no additional trace.

Let \(A(n,v)\) be the largest number of open cells cut out by \(n\) affine hyperplanes in \(\mathbb R^v\). Adding the last hyperplane retains every old cell and splits at most \(A(n-1,v-1)\) of them. Hence
\[
 A(n,v)\le A(n-1,v)+A(n-1,v-1),\qquad
 A(0,v)=A(n,0)=1. \tag{18}
\]
Induction using Pascal's identity gives
\[
 A(n,3)\le\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj. \tag{19}
\]
Restricting to genuine disks, fixing \(h\), restricting centers to \(\mathcal B\), or intersecting a trace with \(\{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t\}\) cannot increase the number of traces. Multiplication by the two choices of \(t\) and by \(|\mathcal H_n|\) proves the cardinality bound.

If \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\), the convention makes both stochastic claims immediate. Otherwise, \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) gives conditional independence of the residuals for almost every score vector, and \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_i\mid X_i]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_P[e^{\lambda\varepsilon_i}\mid X_i]\le e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}. \tag{20}
\]
Complementarity and \(\mathrm{ass:sharp\text{-}assignment}\) ensure that \(T_i=t\) when \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\). Therefore, for nonempty \(S\in\mathscr S_n\) and \(u\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
  \exp\!\left\{u\frac{\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}\right\}
  \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 &=\prod_{i\in S}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
  \exp\!\left\{\frac{u\varepsilon_i}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}\right\}
  \ \middle|\ X_i\right]\\
 &\le\prod_{i\in S}\exp\!\left\{\frac{u^2}{2|S|}\right\}
 =e^{u^2/2}.
 \end{aligned}\tag{21}
\]
For \(Z_S=(\sigma\sqrt{|S|})^{-1}\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i\), the pointwise inequality
\[

and (21), optimized at \(u=z>0\), give

The same calculation for \(-Z_S\), followed by a union bound, yields

 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}|Z_S|>z

 &\le z_0+2|\mathscr S_n|\int_{z_0}^{\infty}e^{-z^2/2}\,dz\\
 &\le z_0+z_0^{-1}\le z_0+1.
 \end{aligned}
\]

payload.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},
 \qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le 2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and the exact conditional Gaussian condition \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), adopt the convention that the maximum below is zero when \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\). For \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-almost every score vector, conditionally on the scores and with \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), one has for every \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le 2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
The conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most
\[
 \sqrt{2\log\{2(1\vee|\mathscr S_n|)\}}+1.
\]

carrier.proof_tex:
We first prove simultaneous coverage.  Fix a member \(P\) of the triangular union.  By \(\mathrm{def:triangular\text{-}profile\text{-}union}\), it belongs to some \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{base}}\), so the exact Gaussian, Lipschitz, bounded-trace, and positive polynomial lower-mass member conditions all hold.  The complement condition on the assignment regions implies that \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\) exactly when \(T_i=t\).  Condition on \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\); the counts and selected bandwidths are then fixed.

For \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<r\le h_0\), polynomial lower mass gives
\[
 P_X\{X\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X,x)\le r\}\ge c_mr^\kappa>0. \tag{10}
\]
Therefore \(x\) belongs to the support of the restricted side measure.  Letting a support point \(z'\) tend to \(x\) in the Lipschitz inequality and using the definition of the trace gives
\[
 |g_{t,P}(z)-\theta_{t,P}(x)|\le Ld(z,x) \tag{11}
\]
for every relevant side-support point \(z\) in the \(h_0\)-tube.  If \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))>0\), every observation in the selected average has distance at most \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\le h_0\) from \(x\).  Averaging (11) therefore yields
\[
 \left|N^{-1}\sum_{i\in S}g_{t,P}(X_i)-\theta_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \le L\widehat h_{t,n}(x). \tag{12}
\]
If \(N=0\), \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}constant\text{-}side\text{-}fit}\) makes the side fit zero, and the bounded-trace member condition bounds its error by \(L\).

By \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\), the number of nonempty averaging sets is at most
\[
 M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Apply that lemma with \(z=\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)}\).  Since \(0<\gamma<1\), its conditional union bound shows that, with conditional probability at least \(1-\gamma\), every nonempty candidate set satisfies
\[
 \left|N^{-1}\sum_{i\in S}\{Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\}\right|
 \le\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)}N}. \tag{13}
\]
Equations (12)--(13), together with the zero-count case, bound each side error by \(B_{t,n}(x)\), simultaneously over \(x\) and \(t\).  The triangle inequality then puts \(\tau_P(x)\) in \(\mathcal C_n(x)\) for every \(x\), conditionally with probability at least \(1-\gamma\).  Integrating over the scores proves the finite-sample guarantee uniformly over the union.  The grid is finite, all counts and fits are Borel functions of the data and \(x\), and the numerical tie-break in \(\widehat h_{t,n}\) is deterministic; hence the displayed interval is data measurable.

We next prove the pervasive expected-width rate directly.  Put
\[
 r=\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), choose \(b\in\mathcal H_n\) such that \(2r\le b<4r\); then \(b/2\in\mathcal H_n\) and \(b<h_0\).  Let \(z_1,\ldots,z_J\) be a maximal \(b/2\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\).  It is a \(b/2\)-net, and the global boundary-entropy member condition gives
\[
 J\le 2C_{\mathcal B}b^{-1}. \tag{14}
\]
For every \(j,t\), independent sampling and polynomial lower mass make \(N_{t,n}(z_j,b/2)\) binomial with mean at least
\[
 \mu_b=nc_m(b/2)^\kappa. \tag{15}
\]
For completeness, if \(N\) is binomial with mean \(\mu=nq\), Markov's inequality applied to \(2^{-N}\) gives
\[
 \Pr\{N\le\mu/2\}
 \le 2^{\mu/2}(1-q/2)^n
 \le e^{-\mu/8}, \tag{16}
\]
because \(1-y\le e^{-y}\) and \((\log2)/2-1/2<-1/8\).  A union bound over (14) shows that the event
\[
 E_b=\bigcap_{j,t}\{N_{t,n}(z_j,b/2)\ge\mu_b/2\}
\]
satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}}P(E_b^c)
 \le 4C_{\mathcal B}b^{-1}e^{-\mu_b/8}. \tag{17}
\]
If \(x\in\mathcal B\), select \(z_j\) with \(d(x,z_j)\le b/2\).  Then \(B(z_j,b/2)\subseteq B(x,b)\), so on \(E_b\),
\[
 \inf_{x\in\mathcal B,\,t\in\{0,1\}}N_{t,n}(x,b)\ge\mu_b/2. \tag{18}
\]
Uniformly for \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\), the quantity \(\mu_b\) grows faster than \(\log(e+n/b)\); indeed, using \(b\ge2r\),
\[
 \mu_b\ge c n^{2/(\kappa+2)}(\log n)^{\kappa/(\kappa+2)}. \tag{19}
\]
Thus (18) exceeds \(8\log(e+n/b)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), and \(b\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\) for every \(x,t\) on \(E_b\).

For an admissible \(u\), write
\[
 Q_{t,x}(u)=Lu+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/u)}{N_{t,n}(x,u)}}.
\]
The minimizing definition of \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\), (18), and \(b\asymp r\) give on \(E_b\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
 Q_{t,x}(\widehat h_{t,n}(x))
 &\le Q_{t,x}(b)\\
 &\le Lb+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(e+n/b)}{\mu_b}}
 \le Cr. \tag{20}
\end{aligned}
\]
The last inequality follows from \(nb^{\kappa+2}\asymp\log n\), with constants uniform over the declared compact exponent range.  Moreover,
\[
 M_n\le Cn^3(1+\log n),
 \qquad
 \log(e+n/\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\ge\log(e+n), \tag{21}
\]
because \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\le h_0<1\).  Since the selected bandwidth is admissible on \(E_b\), its count is positive.  Equations (20)--(21) imply
\[
 \sup_{x,t}B_{t,n}(x)\le Cr \quad\text{on }E_b. \tag{22}
\]
On \(E_b^c\), the definition of \(B_{t,n}\), the bounds \(\widehat h_{t,n}\le h_0<1\) and \(N\ge1\) in its positive-count branch, and (21) give the deterministic envelope
\[
 \sup_{x,t}B_{t,n}(x)\le C(1+\sqrt{\log n}). \tag{23}
\]
The interval construction gives \(W_n(x)=B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\).  Hence (17), (19), and (22)--(23) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 &\le Cr+C(1+\sqrt{\log n})b^{-1}e^{-\mu_b/8}\\
 &\le Cr
 =C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)} \tag{24}
\end{aligned}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The exponential term is \(o(r)\) by (19).  This proves the asserted width rate, including every fallback configuration.

Finally fix \(x\in\mathcal B\) and two laws \(P_0,P_1\) in a class over which the band has simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\).  Let
\[
 A_j=\{\tau_{P_j}(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\},\qquad j=0,1.
\]
Writing \(P_j^{\otimes n}\) for the induced full observed-data experiment, honesty gives \(P_j^{\otimes n}(A_j)\ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\).  The definition of total variation gives
\[
 P_0^{\otimes n}(A_1)
 \ge P_1^{\otimes n}(A_1)-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n}). \tag{25}
\]
The union bound for complements and (25) therefore imply
\[
 P_0^{\otimes n}(A_0\cap A_1)
 \ge1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n}). \tag{26}
\]
On \(A_0\cap A_1\), the interval contains both target values, so
\[
 W_n(x)\ge\frac12|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|. \tag{27}
\]
Multiplying (27) by the positive part of (26) and taking expectation proves the displayed two-law obstruction.

The distance in (25) is the total variation of the full observed experiments.  Score extraction is a measurable map, so data processing gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(P_{0,X}^{\otimes n},P_{1,X}^{\otimes n})
 \le\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n}), \tag{28}
\]
which is the wrong direction for replacing the full distance by the score distance in the lower bound.  Also, (13) uses \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), while the local benchmark can have bounded \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\).  Thus the proved global band and full-law obstruction do not establish either the local-oracle width ratio or the requested score-law necessary-and-sufficient criterion, exactly as stated.

target_declaration.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define
\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),\ 
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
In particular, uniformly over \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\), \(\mathbb E_P\sup_x W_n(x)\le C(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Moreover, for any \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
Thus the frozen assumptions yield an explicit honest global band and a computable two-law width obstruction. They do not by themselves establish the sharper uniform ratio to \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\): the global calibration uses \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), whereas \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\) can be bounded at an isolated thin site. Nor does the displayed two-law argument turn score-law total variation alone into an exact necessary-and-sufficient adaptation criterion without a same-class outcome perturbation whose full observed-law distance is controlled. This is a partial resolution of the honest-adaptation question.
target_declaration.proof_tex:
The partition and sharp-assignment conditions imply \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\) if and only if \(T_i=t\).  Condition on the scores, so all selected bandwidths are fixed.  Polynomial lower mass for every member of the triangular union puts each boundary point in each side support, and Lipschitz smoothness gives, whenever the selected count \(N\) is positive,
\[
 \left|N^{-1}\sum_{i\in S}g_{t,P}(X_i)-\theta_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \le L\widehat h_{t,n}(x). \tag{43}
\]
If \(N=0\), the side fit is zero and the bounded-trace assumption bounds its error by \(L\).

By \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\), at most
\[
 M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj
\]
nonempty averaging sets can occur.  Its Gaussian tail inequality and a union bound imply that, conditionally on the scores, with probability at least \(1-\gamma\), every nonempty candidate set satisfies
\[
 \left|N^{-1}\sum_{i\in S}\{Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\}\right|
 \le\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)}N}. \tag{44}
\]
Equations (43)--(44), and the zero-count bound, show that each side error is at most \(B_{t,n}(x)\), simultaneously over \(x\) and \(t\).  The triangle inequality proves conditional and hence unconditional simultaneous coverage.  All counts and fits are measurable, the grids are finite, and the bandwidth rule has a deterministic tie break, so the displayed band is data measurable.

For the pervasive width assertion, \(\log(2M_n/\gamma)\le C\log n\).  The uniform count event and comparison scale in \(\mathrm{thm:pervasive\text{-}adaptive\text{-}frontier}\) show that, outside an event of probability \(Ch_*^{-1}e^{-cnh_*^{\kappa}}\), the selected bias plus the standard-error term in (44) is bounded by \(Cr_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), uniformly in \(x,t,P\).  On the exceptional event it is at most \(L+\sigma\sqrt{C\log n}\); its expected contribution is \(o(r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\).  Since the constructed interval has
\[
 W_n(x)=B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x),
\]
the asserted expected supremum width follows.

For the obstruction, fix \(x\in\mathcal B\) and let \(A_j\) be the event that \(\mathcal C_n(x)\) contains \(\tau_{P_j}(x)\).  Honesty gives
\[
 P_j(A_j)\ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n,
 \qquad j=0,1.
\]
By the definition of total variation,
\[
 P_0(A_1)\ge P_1(A_1)-\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n}).
\]
Therefore
\[
 P_0(A_0\cap A_1)
 \ge1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n}). \tag{45}
\]
On \(A_0\cap A_1\), the interval contains both target values, so its half-width is at least half their separation.  Multiplying this deterministic implication by the positive part of (45) and taking \(P_0\)-expectations proves
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
This uses the total variation of the full observed experiments.  A score marginal is only a measurable projection, so its total variation cannot furnish the needed upper bound on the full distance without an additional same-class outcome construction.  Likewise, the global calibration in (44) has \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), whereas the local benchmark may have bounded \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\).  The proved statements therefore establish the advertised global band and two-law obstruction, but not the explicitly disclaimed local-ratio or score-only equivalence.

semantic_closure.construction: \(\widehat\tau_n(x)=\widehat g_{1,n}(x;\widehat h_{1,n}(x))-\widehat g_{0,n}(x;\widehat h_{0,n}(x))\) for \(x\in\mathcal B\).

semantic_closure.statement:
For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},\qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le 2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), conditionally on the scores, if \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), then for every \(z>0\)
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}\frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z\ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2},
\]
and the conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most \(\sqrt{2\log\{2|\mathscr S_n|\}}+1\).
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
For a disk with center \(c\in\mathbb R^2\) and radius \(r\), membership of a fixed point \(x_i\) is equivalent to
\[
 2c^{\mathsf T}x_i+s\ge\|x_i\|_2^2,
 \qquad s=r^2-\|c\|_2^2.
\]
Thus every disk trace is a sign pattern induced by \(n\) affine planes in the three-dimensional parameter \((c_1,c_2,s)\).  A trace realized by a closed disk can be made strict by increasing its radius by less than the positive minimum distance to the finitely many excluded points, so boundary equalities add no patterns.

Let \(A(n,v)\) be the largest number of open cells cut out by \(n\) affine hyperplanes in \(\mathbb R^v\).  Adding the last hyperplane preserves every old cell and splits at most \(A(n-1,v-1)\) cells, because the induced arrangement on that hyperplane has dimension \(v-1\).  Hence
\[
 A(n,v)\le A(n-1,v)+A(n-1,v-1),
 \qquad A(0,v)=A(n,0)=1.
\]
Induction using Pascal's identity gives
\[
 A(n,3)\le\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj. \tag{39}
\]
Restricting the parameter to genuine disks, fixing a radius, restricting centers to \(\mathcal B\), or intersecting every range with the fixed set of indices satisfying \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\) cannot increase the number of traces.  Multiplying (39) by the two sides and by \(|\mathcal H_n|\) proves
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]

By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), conditionally on the scores, the residuals occurring in any member of \(\mathscr S_n\) are independent \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\).  Consequently, for each nonempty \(S\),
\[
 \frac{\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}\sim\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
For \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), completing the square in the exponential-moment bound gives \(\Pr(|Z|>z)\le2e^{-z^2/2}\).  A union bound, which does not require independence between the different set-indexed sums, therefore gives
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}\frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
Finally, integrating this tail from \(z_0=\sqrt{2\log\{2|\mathscr S_n|\}}\), and using \(\int_{z_0}^{\infty}e^{-z^2/2}\,dz\le z_0^{-1}e^{-z_0^2/2}\) when \(z_0>0\), bounds the conditional expectation by \(z_0+1\), as claimed.

semantic_closure.statement: Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). The estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the score density. Uniformly for \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}\mathbb E_P[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|]\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and \(R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). Its fallback event obeys \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}P\{\exists x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}:\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\}\le Cn^3\exp\{-c n c_m h_0^{\kappa}\}\), and this event's contribution is included in the expected-risk bound.
semantic_closure.justification: This closes the same-class upper and lower frontier in the pervasive polynomial regime while controlling the operational empty-admissible-set fallback.
semantic_closure.gap: Gaiffas2007SharpSupNorm gives an unknown-density, spatially varying sup-norm estimator and an inhomogeneous band for a positive continuous univariate design, Gaiffas2007PointwiseAdaptive adapts at one query point, Gaiffas2009Uniform treats finitely many univariate density zeros, and AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 uses known design density and global \(L^2\) loss; none handles vanishing mass on two assignment sides uniformly along a boundary with a same-modulus \(h^{-1}\)-site converse.
semantic_closure.consumer: The \(R\), Python, and Stata \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflows can use observed-count bandwidths that widen automatically in depleted boundary segments and have a specified safe fallback.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
The partition and sharp assignment imply \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\) if and only if \(T_i=t\).  Inspection of \(\mathrm{def:empirical\text{-}counts}\), \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}constant\text{-}side\text{-}fit}\), \(\mathrm{def:admissible\text{-}bandwidths}\), \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\), and \(\mathrm{def:mass\text{-}adaptive\text{-}estimator}\) shows that \(\widehat\tau_n\) is measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\), the known geometry, \(L\), \(\sigma\), and \(n\), and uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the score density.

Fix \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\), and put
\[
 r=\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the dyadic grid contains \(h_*\) with
\[
 r\le h_*<2r. \tag{28}
\]
Take a maximal \(h_*/2\)-separated boundary net.  It has at most \(2C_{\mathcal B}h_*^{-1}\) points by global boundary entropy.  If a net point \(z_j\) is within \(h_*/2\) of \(x\), then \(B(z_j,h_*/2)\subseteq B(x,h_*)\).  Polynomial lower mass therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E_PN_{t,n}(z_j,h_*/2)\ge nc_m(h_*/2)^{\kappa}. \tag{29}
\]
Apply the binomial inequality (21) to all center-side counts.  Ball inclusion then yields an event \(G_n\) on which, simultaneously in \(x\in\mathcal B\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 N_{t,n}(x,h_*)\ge c nc_mh_*^{\kappa},
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}P(G_n^c)
 \le Ch_*^{-1}e^{-cnc_mh_*^{\kappa}}. \tag{30}
\]
Uniformly over \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\),
\[
 \frac{nh_*^{\kappa}}{\log(e+n/h_*)}
 \ge c\left(\frac n{\log n}\right)^{2/(\overline\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{31}
\]
Thus \(h_*\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\) everywhere on \(G_n\), for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The minimizing property of the selected bandwidth, (28), and \(nr^{\kappa+2}=\log n\) imply
\[
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/\widehat h_{t,n}(x))}{N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))}}
 \le Cr. \tag{32}
\]

Condition on the scores.  Polynomial lower mass puts every boundary point in both side supports exactly as in (11), so the trace identity (12) applies.  If the selected count \(N\) is nonzero, Lipschitz smoothness gives
\[
 \left|N^{-1}\sum_{i\in S_{t,x,\widehat h}}g_{t,P}(X_i)-\theta_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \le L\widehat h_{t,n}(x). \tag{33}
\]
Let
\[
 Z_n=\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\{Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\}|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\) and \(|\mathcal H_n|\le2+\log_2n\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P(Z_n\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)\le C\sqrt{\log n}. \tag{34}
\]
Every selected nonempty set belongs to \(\mathscr S_n\).  Since \(h\le h_0<1\) implies \(\log(e+n/h)\ge\log n\), equations (32)--(34), followed by the triangle inequality over the two sides, show that the conditional expected sup loss is at most \(Cr\) on \(G_n\).

On \(G_n^c\), a selected set comes from either an admissible bandwidth or the fallback \(h_0\).  The trace bound and Lipschitz smoothness bound the conditional mean of every nonempty fit by \(L(1+h_0)<2L\), while an empty fit is zero.  Equation (34), with \(|S|^{-1/2}\le1\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 \le C\{L+\sigma\sqrt{\log n}\}. \tag{35}
\]
Using (30)--(35) and (31),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le Cr+C\{L+\sigma\sqrt{\log n}\}h_*^{-1}e^{-cnc_mh_*^{\kappa}}
 \le Cr. \tag{36}
\]
The constants can be chosen uniformly in \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\), because (31) gives a common diverging lower bound for the exponential argument.

The lower bound is the pervasive construction proved in \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), with the explicit circular family certified by \(\mathrm{lem:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}validity}\).  Choosing its scale as \(a_0r\) gives packing logarithm bounded below by a fixed multiple of \(\log n\), uniformly over the compact exponent range, while the product divergence is at most \(Ca_0^{\kappa+2}\log n\le Ca_0^4\log n\).  A fixed sufficiently small \(a_0\) and \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), as used in that theorem, yield
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge cr. \tag{37}
\]

It remains to verify the explicit fallback probability.  Take a maximal \(h_0/2\)-separated boundary net; it has at most \(2C_{\mathcal B}/h_0\) points.  At every center and side the expected radius-\(h_0/2\) count is at least \(nc_m(h_0/2)^{\kappa}\).  Uniformly in the exponent range, this is eventually at least \(16\log(e+n/h_0)\).  The binomial inequality (21), a union bound, and ball inclusion show that, outside an event of probability at most
\[
 C\exp\{-cnc_mh_0^{\kappa}\}, \tag{38}
\]
one has \(N_{t,n}(x,h_0)\ge8\log(e+n/h_0)\) for every \(x,t\).  Hence \(h_0\) is admissible everywhere and no fallback occurs.  Enlarging \(C\), (38) implies the stated \(Cn^3\exp\{-cnc_mh_0^{\kappa}\}\) bound.  Equation (35) and the sharper event estimate in (30) show that the fallback contribution is already included in (36).  Equations (36)--(38) prove the theorem.

semantic_closure.name: \mathcal C_n
semantic_closure.def: A band to be derived from the handle in \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}band\text{-}handle}\).

semantic_closure.name: W_n
semantic_closure.def: \(W_n(x)=\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal C_n(x))/2\).

semantic_closure.name: n
semantic_closure.def: The number of independently sampled units.

semantic_closure.name: \gamma
semantic_closure.def: The target simultaneous miscoverage probability.

semantic_closure.name: \mathcal A_0
semantic_closure.def: The known region assigned to control.

semantic_closure.name: \mathcal A_1
semantic_closure.def: The known region assigned to treatment.

semantic_closure.name: \mathcal H_n
semantic_closure.def: \(\mathcal H_n=\{2^{-j}h_0:0\le j\le\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\}\).

semantic_closure.name: N_{t,n}
semantic_closure.def: \(N_{t,n}(x,h)=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\}\).

semantic_closure.name: t
semantic_closure.def: The index for the control and treatment sides of the assignment boundary.

semantic_closure.name: \widehat h_{t,n}
semantic_closure.def: The measurable bandwidth constructed in \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\), including its empty-set fallback.

semantic_closure.name: L
semantic_closure.def: A fixed envelope for side-regression Lipschitz constants and boundary traces.

semantic_closure.name: \sigma
semantic_closure.def: The conditional Gaussian noise standard deviation.

semantic_closure.name: \widehat\tau_n
semantic_closure.def: The difference of the two count-adaptive observed-side fits constructed in \(\mathrm{def:mass\text{-}adaptive\text{-}estimator}\).

semantic_closure.name: \tau_P
semantic_closure.def: \(\tau_P(x)=\theta_{1,P}(x)-\theta_{0,P}(x)\).

semantic_closure.name: \mathcal B
semantic_closure.def: \(\mathcal B=\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal A_0)\cap\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal A_1)\).

semantic_closure.name: \mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)
semantic_closure.type: nonempty triangular union of law classes
semantic_closure.def: The union constructed in \(\mathrm{def:triangular\text{-}profile\text{-}union}\).

semantic_closure.name: \Lambda_n
semantic_closure.def: A declared collection of exponents and lower--upper packing profiles for which the triangular union in \(\mathrm{def:triangular\text{-}profile\text{-}union}\) is nonempty.

semantic_closure.name: P
semantic_closure.def: A law for the potential outcomes and score that induces the observed law of \(O\).

semantic_closure.name: \kappa
semantic_closure.def: The exponent governing polynomial depletion of one-sided boundary-neighborhood mass.

semantic_closure.name: \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
semantic_closure.def: The class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:pervasive\text{-}thinning\text{-}class}\).

semantic_closure.name: r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
semantic_closure.def: \(r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}=(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\).

semantic_closure.def: \(\operatorname{TV}(Q,Q')=\sup_E|Q(E)-Q'(E)|\).

semantic_closure.def: The oracle benchmark constructed in \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}oracle\text{-}benchmark}\).

semantic_closure.def: \(K_P(x,h)=1\vee\mathsf J_P(h,a_P(x,h))\).

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), use the circular inside--outside assignment and constants certified by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), and suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\).  Put \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare
\[
 \mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=\mathbf 1\{u\ge C_mh^\kappa\},
 \qquad 0<h\le h_0,\quad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\cup
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}),
\]
and there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \le R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \le C\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 {r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Therefore \(\mathrm{oeq:arbitrary\text{-}modulus\text{-}frontier}\) has a negative answer as stated: a class constrained only by a lower mass modulus and a lower thin-site packing declaration cannot both retain the pervasive subclass and recover the isolated polynomial frontier when the declared multiplicity is one.  To formulate an arbitrary-modulus result that distinguishes the two regimes, one must add an upper thin-site packing restriction or use an intrinsic two-sided profile; under the frozen two-argument class, the requested package of conclusions cannot hold.
semantic_closure.justification: This theorem gives an explicit same-class polynomial witness for which a constant declared lower packing profile nevertheless has the pervasive logarithmic minimax rate.
semantic_closure.gap: An exact arbitrary-modulus frontier for a refined class with upper as well as lower thin-site packing control remains unresolved; the frozen two-argument class cannot express the isolated side of that comparison.
semantic_closure.consumer: The \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflow must not interpret a constant lower packing declaration as evidence of isolated thinning; it needs an upper-profile certificate before using an isolated-rate guarantee.

semantic_closure.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and \(m(r)>0\) for every \(0<r\le h_0\). For every nonempty class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\), let \(\overline\tau_n(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\widehat\tau_n(x)\}\), where \(\Pi_I\) is Euclidean projection onto the interval \(I\). There are constants \(A,C,c,a>0\), depending only on the fixed envelopes, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\min\left[ L,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\\nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)}}
 \left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}\right],
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). The estimator in this display uses neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\); they occur only in its guarantee. Conversely, if \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\), then
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh
\]
whenever either \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), or \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\). Hence a sufficient uniform-consistency condition for a sequence of nonempty such classes with lower moduli \(m_n\) is the existence of \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\); a necessary condition is that the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible values of \(h\) in the preceding display tends to zero. For a fixed positive exponential modulus \(m_\alpha\), the sufficient condition holds. With polynomial profiles, the lower display yields the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp1\) and the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp h^{-1}\); together with \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), these rates are exact. For an arbitrary slack lower packing declaration, the lower display need not match the upper display based on global boundary entropy, so this is a proved two-sided bracket, not an assertion of an unproved exact arbitrary-profile criterion.
semantic_closure.justification: This theorem gives an explicit count-based global upper map and a legal same-class Lipschitz-tent converse indexed by the declared lower packing profile.
semantic_closure.gap: The two sides match in the isolated and pervasive polynomial regimes. For arbitrary declarations they can differ because \(\mathsf J_{-}\) may be slack while the upper argument covers the full boundary using global entropy.
semantic_closure.consumer: The \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflow can check the sufficient count condition before fitting and report a lower testing experiment when uniform consistency is impossible.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
For a law \(P\) in the revised class, define the finite one-sided score measure
\[
 \mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t).
\]
If \(x\in\mathcal B\) and \(r>0\), set \(s=\min\{h_0,r/2\}\). Positivity of \(m\) and \(\mathrm{ass:declared\text{-}modulus\text{-}lower\text{-}mass}\), which is a member property of \(\mathrm{def:modulus\text{-}profile\text{-}class}\), give
\[
 \mu_{t,P}\{z:d(z,x)<r\}\ge q_{t,P}(x,s)\ge m(s)>0. \tag{40}
\]
Thus \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) on both sides. The unique Lipschitz representative and the definition of its trace consequently give
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x). \tag{41}
\]
Under \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), sharp assignment makes \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\) equivalent to \(T_i=t\). Therefore the conditional mean of each observed side average is the corresponding average of \(g_{t,P}(X_i)\). The bounded-trace member property yields \(\tau_P(x)\in[-2L,2L]\); projection onto this closed interval cannot increase pointwise distance to \(\tau_P(x)\), and the clipped loss is at most \(4L\).

We prove the upper display. Fix \(h\) with \(h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\) and \(nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)\). Let \(z_1,\ldots,z_K\) be a maximal \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\). It is an \(h\)-net, and \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) gives \(K\le C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}\). For each \(j,t\), \(N_{t,n}(z_j,h)\) is binomial with success probability \(q_{t,P}(z_j,h)\ge m(h)\), by independent sampling and the class's lower-mass property. If \(N\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), then Markov's inequality applied to \(2^{-N}\) gives
\[
 \Pr\{N\le nq/2\}
 \le 2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n
 \le \exp(-nq/8), \tag{42}
\]
where the last inequality follows from \(1-y\le e^{-y}\) and \((\log2)/2-1/2<-1/8\). Hence a union bound, monotonicity in the threshold, and \(q\ge m(h)\) show
\[
 \Pr_P(H_h^c)\le 2C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}, \tag{43}
\]
where \(H_h\) is the event on which all \(N_{t,n}(z_j,h)\ge nm(h)/2\). For every \(x\in\mathcal B\), select a net point \(z_j\) with \(d(x,z_j)\le h\). The inclusion \(B(z_j,h)\subseteq B(x,2h)\) implies on \(H_h\) that
\[
 \inf_{x\in\mathcal B,\,t\in\{0,1\}}N_{t,n}(x,2h)\ge nm(h)/2. \tag{44}
\]
Choose the constant \(A\) so that the right-hand side of (44) is at least \(8\log(e+n/(2h))\). Then \(2h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\) for every \(x,t\) on \(H_h\).

Condition on the scores. For any selected nonempty averaging set at \((x,b,t)\), Lipschitz smoothness and (41) give
\[
 \left|\frac1{N_{t,n}(x,b)}\sum_{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le b}g_{t,P}(X_i)-\theta_{t,P}(x)\right|\le Lb. \tag{45}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\), simultaneously over every candidate disk pattern, the conditional expected normalized Gaussian error is at most
\[
 \sqrt{2\log\!\left(4|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\right)}+1\le C\sqrt{\log(e+n)}. \tag{46}
\]
Because every \(b\in\mathcal H_n\) satisfies \(b\le h_0<1\), \(\log(e+n)\le C\log(e+n/b)\). Combining (45)--(46) with the minimizing property in \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\), and comparing the selected criterion to the admissible candidate \(2h\), gives on \(H_h\)
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 \le C\left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}. \tag{47}
\]
Here both side errors have been added, and (44) was used in the stochastic term. Projection leaves the error no larger. On \(H_h^c\), the clipped error is at most \(4L\). Equations (43) and (47) therefore yield
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}
   +CLh^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}. \tag{48}
\]
Increasing \(A\), if necessary, makes the last term at most \(CLh\), since \(e^{-nm(h)/8}\le(e+n/h)^{-A/8}\). The deterministic clipped bound supplies the first argument \(L\) of the minimum when no scale qualifies. Taking the infimum over qualifying dyadic pairs proves the upper bracket. The sample map in \(\mathrm{def:mass\text{-}adaptive\text{-}estimator}\) and the projection use neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\).

We next prove the lower display within the same class. Choose any member \(P^\circ\) of the assumed nonempty class and retain its score marginal and assignment geometry. On an extension carrying independent standard normal variables \(Z_0,Z_1\), define a baseline law \(P_0\) by \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\). The score-dependent class properties are unchanged, while the side regressions and traces are zero, so the response smoothness, boundedness, Gaussian-error, sharp-assignment, and consistency properties all hold. Thus \(P_0\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\).

Let \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\ge1\). The class's lower-profile property and the definition of \(\mathsf J_P\) supply \(h\)-separated points \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) for which \(a_{P_0}(x_j,h)\le u\). Choose \(t_j\) attaining this minimum and put
\[
 \eta_h=\frac{Lh}{12},\qquad
 \psi_{j,h}(z)=\left(1-\frac{3d(z,x_j)}h\right)_+.
\]
Define \(P_j\) by retaining the baseline score law and errors and shifting only the potential outcome on side \(t_j\): add \(\eta_h\psi_{j,h}(X)\) when \(t_j=1\), and subtract it when \(t_j=0\). The added regression is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz because \(\psi_{j,h}\) is \(3/h\)-Lipschitz; its absolute trace is at most \(Lh/12<L\), since \(h\le h_0<1\). All design properties remain unchanged, and the error around the shifted conditional mean is still \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\). Hence every \(P_j\) belongs to \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\).

By (40)--(41), each center is in both one-sided supports and the target shift at \(x_j\) equals \(\eta_h\). If \(k\ne j\), then \(d(x_j,x_k)\ge h\), so \(\psi_{k,h}(x_j)=0\). Consequently
\[
 \|\tau_{P_j}-\tau_{P_k}\|_\infty\ge\eta_h,
 \qquad 0\le j<k\le M. \tag{49}
\]
Conditionally on a score value on the perturbed assignment side, the observed outcome changes from a normal mean zero to a normal mean \(s_j\eta_h\psi_{j,h}(X)\), with \(s_j\in\{-1,1\}\), and it does not change elsewhere. Direct integration of the Gaussian log-likelihood ratio gives conditional relative entropy \(\eta_h^2\psi_{j,h}(X)^2/(2\sigma^2)\). Since the tent is supported inside \(B(x_j,h/3)\subseteq B(x_j,h)\),
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 =\frac{n\eta_h^2}{2\sigma^2}\int\psi_{j,h}(z)^2\,d\mu_{t_j,P_0}(z)
 \le \frac{nL^2h^2u}{288\sigma^2}. \tag{50}
\]
If the first information condition holds, retain any one alternative and apply the two-law clause of \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), decreasing the numerical \(a\) so that (50) is at most \(1/8\). If \(M\ge2\) and the logarithmic condition holds, choose \(a\) so small that (50) is at most the multiple-law threshold times \(\log M\); this is possible uniformly over \(M\ge2\) because \(\log(M+1)/\log M\le\log3/\log2\). Applying the same lemma with the sup metric and \(2\delta=\eta_h\) proves \(R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh\).

For a sequence of nonempty classes, suppose \(h_n\downarrow0\), \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), and
\[
 \frac{nm_n(h_n)}{\log(e+n/h_n)}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{51}
\]
Then the eligibility condition holds eventually, \(Lh_n\to0\), and the square-root term in (48) tends to zero. This proves sufficient uniform consistency. Conversely, if the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible radii does not tend to zero, then along a subsequence one may choose feasible radii bounded below by a fixed positive constant (or half that constant when the supremum is not attained). The lower display then keeps the minimax risk bounded below by a positive constant, proving the stated necessary condition.

For \(m_\alpha\), \(\mathrm{prop:exponential\text{-}horn\text{-}consistency}\) supplies positivity and
\(m_\alpha(h)\asymp h^{\alpha+1}e^{-h^{-\alpha}}\). Set \(s_n=\{(\log n)/2\}^{-1/\alpha}\). Then
\[
 \frac{nm_\alpha(s_n)}{\log(e+n/s_n)}
 \asymp
 \frac{n^{1/2}s_n^{\alpha+1}}{\log n}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{52}
\]
Round \(s_n\) upward to the next point \(h_n\) of the dyadic grid. Eventually \(s_n\le h_n<2s_n\), both \(h_n\) and \(2h_n\) belong to \(\mathcal H_n\), and monotonicity of \(m_\alpha\) preserves (52). Thus the sufficient condition holds for the fixed exponential horn.

For polynomial profiles, set \(u=C_mh^\kappa\). If \(M\asymp1\), (50) is bounded at \(h\asymp n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\). If \(M\asymp h^{-1}\), the logarithmic information condition is met at \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), because \(nh^{\kappa+2}\asymp\log(1/h)\). The matching achievability bounds in \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\) make both rates exact.

Finally, the two generic displays can differ because the declared lower packing profile may be slack while the upper proof covers the entire boundary. On the circular pervasive witness, take \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=0\) for \(u<C_mh^\kappa\) and \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=1\) for \(u\ge C_mh^\kappa\). By \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), after choosing its fixed constants this defines a nonempty class containing the pervasive witness. Its declared lower profile exposes only \(M=1\), whereas (48) uses the global boundary entropy and therefore carries the global logarithm. This legal declaration certifies the stated possible gap and completes the two-sided bracket.

semantic_closure.statement: Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), an assignment geometry satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) and \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), and constants for which \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) are nonempty; \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) supplies an explicit such specification. The two classes share the scalar lower modulus \(c_mh^{\kappa}\), but there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). Thus no expected-sup minimax frontier is a functional of the common scalar modulus alone, and the frontier separates according to the declared thin-site multiplicity profile.
semantic_closure.justification: The theorem identifies multiplicity of thin locations, rather than local mass at the single worst point, as the missing information coordinate for uniform boundary estimation.
semantic_closure.gap: Gaiffas2007SharpSupNorm gives an unknown-density, spatially normalized univariate sup-norm estimator under a positive continuous design density, Gaiffas2009Uniform treats finitely many univariate density zeros, and AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 studies known-design global \(L^2\) loss; none gives a same-modulus isolated-versus-pervasive expected-sup separation for a two-sided causal boundary.
semantic_closure.consumer: Users of the full boundary causal trace curve can distinguish one local data desert from boundary-wide depletion before interpreting a worst-case uniform rate.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
For a law \(P\), define the finite one-sided score measure
\[
 \mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t).
\]
If \(P\) belongs to either class, \(x\in\mathcal B\), and \(r>0\), put \(s=\min\{h_0,r/2\}\).  By \(h_0>0\), \(c_m>0\), and \(\mathrm{ass:polynomial\text{-}lower\text{-}mass}\),
\[
 \mu_{t,P}\{z:d(z,x)<r\}\ge q_{t,P}(x,s)\ge c_ms^{\kappa}>0. \tag{11}
\]
Thus \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\).  The repaired definition of \(g_{t,P}\), the Lipschitz assumption, and the definition of the trace imply
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x). \tag{12}
\]
Under \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), sharp assignment makes \(X\in\mathcal A_t\) equivalent to \(T=t\), so all averages below have conditional observed-outcome mean \(g_{t,P}(X)\).  Consistency supplies the causal interpretation on these assignment-compatible sides; the statistical calculations use only the observed regression.

We first prove the lower bounds by subexperiments inside the same classes.  Begin with any member of the nonempty class under consideration and retain its score law and geometry.  On an extension carrying independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), set \(Y(s)=\sigma Z_s\), \(s\in\{0,1\}\), to obtain a baseline law \(Q_0\).  Its regressions and traces vanish.  The design conditions are unchanged, while the response conditions follow directly, so \(Q_0\) remains in the same class.

For the isolated class take
\[
 h=a_0n^{-1/(\kappa+2)},
\]
where \(a_0>0\) is chosen below.  For large \(n\), \(h\le h_0/3\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}site}\) and the definition of \(\mathsf J_P\) provide \(x_h\in\mathcal B\) and \(t_h\in\{0,1\}\) such that
\[
 q_{t_h,P}(x_h,h)=a_P(x_h,h)\le C_mh^{\kappa}. \tag{13}
\]
Set
\[
 \psi_h(z)=\left(1-\frac{3d(z,x_h)}h\right)_+,
 \qquad \eta_h=\frac{Lh}{12}.
\]
If \(t_h=1\), shift \(Y(1)\) upward by \(\eta_h\psi_h(X)\); if \(t_h=0\), shift \(Y(0)\) downward by the same amount, leaving the other potential outcome unshifted.  The perturbation is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz, is bounded by \(L\), preserves the score law, and preserves Gaussian errors.  Hence the resulting law \(Q_1\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\).  By (12),
\[
 \|\tau_{Q_1}-\tau_{Q_0}\|_{\infty}\ge\eta_h. \tag{14}
\]
Using the Gaussian identity (8), the support of the tent, and (13),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)
 &=\frac{\eta_h^2}{2\sigma^2}\int\psi_h(z)^2\,d\mu_{t_h,P}(z)\\
 &\le\frac{C_mL^2}{288\sigma^2}h^{\kappa+2}. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{15}
\]
Additivity of relative entropy for product measures gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})\le Ca_0^{\kappa+2}.
\]
Choose \(a_0\) so that this is at most \(1/8\).  The two-law clause of \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), applied with the sup metric and \(2\delta=\eta_h\), gives
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}})
 \ge c n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}=c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}. \tag{16}
\]

For the pervasive class take
\[
 h=a_0\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
For large \(n\), \(h\le h_0/3\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:pervasive\text{-}thin\text{-}sites}\) supplies \(h\)-separated points \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) with
\[
 M\ge c_Jh^{-1},\qquad a_P(x_j,h)\le C_mh^{\kappa}. \tag{17}
\]
Finiteness follows from \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\).  Choose at each point a side attaining the minimum, and perturb that side with a radius-\(h/3\), height-\(Lh/12\) tent, upward on side one and downward on side zero.  The preceding membership argument gives laws \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_M\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\).  The supports of distinct tents do not contain the other centers, so their target curves are pairwise separated by at least \(Lh/12\) in sup norm.  The calculation in (15) gives
\[
 \max_{1\le j\le M}\operatorname{KL}(Q_j^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le Cnh^{\kappa+2}=Ca_0^{\kappa+2}\log n. \tag{18}
\]
For fixed \(\kappa\), (17) implies \(\log M\ge c_{\kappa}\log n\) eventually.  Choose \(a_0\) small enough that (18) is at most \(a\log M\), with \(a<1/8\).  The multiple-law clause of \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\) yields
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})
 \ge c\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}
 =c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}. \tag{19}
\]

We next give genuine data-driven upper bounds.  Fix \(0<b\le h_0/2\), and choose a deterministic maximal \(b/2\)-separated set \(z_1,\ldots,z_M\) in \(\mathcal B\).  It is a \(b/2\)-net, and global boundary entropy gives \(M\le2C_{\mathcal B}b^{-1}\).  Let \(j(x)\) be the least index with \(d(x,z_{j(x)})\le b/2\), and define
\[
 K_{t,j}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,d(X_i,z_j)\le b\},
\]
\[
 \overline g_{t,j}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^nY_i\mathbf1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,d(X_i,z_j)\le b\}}{K_{t,j}\vee1},
 \qquad
 \widetilde\tau_{n,b}(x)=\overline g_{1,j(x)}-\overline g_{0,j(x)}.
\]
This is one estimator measurable in the sample and known geometry.  On \(K_{t,j(x)}>0\), equations (11)--(12) and Lipschitz smoothness imply
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_P(\overline g_{t,j(x)}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)-\theta_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \le\frac{3Lb}{2}. \tag{20}
\]

We shall use the following elementary count calculation.  If \(N\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), Markov's inequality applied to \(2^{-N}\) and \(1-y\le e^{-y}\) give
\[
 \Pr(N\le nq/2)
 \le2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n
 \le e^{-nq/8}. \tag{21}
\]
For the pervasive upper bound set \(b=r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\).  Polynomial lower mass, (21), and a union bound give an event \(H_b\) on which every \(K_{t,j}\ge nc_mb^{\kappa}/2\) and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}P(H_b^c)
 \le Cb^{-1}e^{-cnc_mb^{\kappa}}. \tag{22}
\]
Conditionally on the scores and on \(H_b\), Gaussian errors and a union bound over \(2M\) averages give
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left[
 \max_{t,j}|\overline g_{t,j}-\mathbb E_P(\overline g_{t,j}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)|
 \mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 \le C\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e/b)}{nc_mb^{\kappa}}}. \tag{23}
\]
Since \(nb^{\kappa+2}=\log n\), the right side is at most \(C_{\kappa}b\).  On \(H_b^c\), bounded traces and Lipschitz smoothness bound every conditional mean by \(L(1+h_0)<2L\), while a Gaussian union bound bounds the conditional expected maximum noise by \(C\sigma\sqrt{\log(e/b)}\).  Combining (20)--(23) gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\|\widetilde\tau_{n,b}-\tau_P\|_{\infty}
 \le C_{\kappa}b+C\{L+\sigma\sqrt{\log(e/b)}\}b^{-1}e^{-cnc_mb^{\kappa}}
 \le C_{\kappa}b. \tag{24}
\]

For the isolated upper bound set \(b=r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\), so \(nb^{\kappa}=b^{-2}\).  Fix a side, choose \(D\ge C_m\), put \(u_{\ell}=\min\{1,D2^{\ell}b^{\kappa}\}\), and group net centers according as \(q_{t,P}(z_j,b)\le u_0\) or \(u_{\ell-1}<q_{t,P}(z_j,b)\le u_{\ell}\).  Every center in group \(\ell\) obeys
\[
 a_P(z_j,b/2)\le q_{t,P}(z_j,b)\le u_{\ell}.
\]
Applying the isolated profile upper bound at radius \(b/2\), and the global entropy bound for the terminal group, yields
\[
 M_{\ell}\le C_{\kappa}\{1+2^{\ell/(\kappa-2)}\}. \tag{25}
\]
In group zero, polynomial lower mass makes the mean count at least \(c_mb^{-2}\); in group \(\ell\ge1\), it exceeds \(D2^{\ell-1}b^{-2}\).  Equations (21) and (25), summed over groups and sides, give an event \(H_b\) such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}P(H_b^c)
 \le C_{\kappa}\sum_{\ell\ge0}\{1+2^{\ell/(\kappa-2)}\}e^{-cb^{-2}2^{\ell}}
 \le C_{\kappa}e^{-c_{\kappa}/b^2}. \tag{26}
\]
On \(H_b\), a Gaussian union bound at threshold \(zb\) gives
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{
 \max_{t,j}|\overline g_{t,j}-\mathbb E_P(\overline g_{t,j}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)|>zb
 \mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le C_{\kappa}\sum_{\ell\ge0}\{1+2^{\ell/(\kappa-2)}\}e^{-cz^22^{\ell}}.
\]
The series is at most \(C_{\kappa}e^{-c_{\kappa}z^2}\) for all sufficiently large fixed \(z\); integration gives conditional expected stochastic maximum \(O_{\kappa}(b)\).  Equation (20) gives bias \(O(b)\), and the bad-event contribution is \(o(b)\) by (26) and the same Gaussian maximum bound used after (23).  Therefore
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 \mathbb E_P\|\widetilde\tau_{n,b}-\tau_P\|_{\infty}
 \le C_{\kappa}b. \tag{27}
\]
The definition of \(R_n\), applied to (24) and (27), proves both upper bounds.  Together with (16) and (19), this proves both matched rates.  The explicit nonempty circular specifications are supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), while \(\mathrm{lem:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}validity}\) independently certifies concrete legal lower families.  Since the common scalar modulus is \(c_mh^{\kappa}\) but the rates differ by \((\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), the scalar modulus alone cannot determine the expected-sup frontier.

semantic_closure.name: expected-sup minimax risk
semantic_closure.construction: For a nonempty law class \(\mathcal P\), \(R_n(\mathcal P)=\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widetilde\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|]\), where the infimum is over estimators measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\) and the known assignment geometry.

semantic_closure.statement: For all sufficiently small \(h\), every law in \(\{\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}:0\le j\le|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), the packing size satisfies \(|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\asymp h^{-1}\), and every pair has \(\operatorname{KL}((\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n},(\mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n})\le CnL^2h^{\kappa+2}/\sigma^2\). The two laws \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,0,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,1,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and their \(n\)-fold products obey the same divergence bound. At an active site, their traces are \(\theta_{1,P}(x_j)=Lh/4\), \(\theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-Lh/4\), and \(\tau_P(x_j)=Lh/2\).
semantic_closure.justification: This lemma certifies the packed lower experiment inside the same classes used by the upper bounds and states its pairwise information budget.
semantic_closure.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate uses local univariate bumps, while the present family perturbs both identified boundary sides at many separated sites without changing the common score-mass modulus.
semantic_closure.consumer: The minimax lower theorem can invoke a concrete Fano family for pervasive thinning and a concrete Le Cam pair for isolated thinning.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
The distance map \(z\mapsto d(z,x_j)\) is one-Lipschitz.  Thus
\[
 \psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+
\]
is \(h^{-1}\)-Lipschitz, and each perturbed side regression in \(\mathrm{def:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}family}\) is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz.  Its absolute trace is at most \(Lh/4\le L\) for sufficiently small \(h\).  The perturbation changes neither the score law nor any local mass or packing profile.  The Gaussian-error, sharp-assignment, and consistency conditions follow from the construction.  Therefore \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) and the two class definitions put every pervasive perturbation in \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and both isolated perturbations in \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\).

Maximality of the \(3h\)-separated set implies that arcs of radius \(3h\) cover \(S^1\), while arcs of radius \(3h/2\) about its points are disjoint.  Comparing total arclength with \(2\pi\) gives
\[
 c h^{-1}\le |\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\le C h^{-1}. \tag{7}
\]

Put \(a=Lh/4\).  Conditional on \(X=z\), the observed Gaussian outcome under alternatives \(j\) and \(k\) has a common variance \(\sigma^2\), and the difference of its means has absolute value \(a|\psi_{j,h}(z)-\psi_{k,h}(z)|\), irrespective of the assigned side.  For the full potential-outcome vector, the two independent coordinates contribute the same quantity and only double the bound below.  Direct integration of two univariate Gaussian densities gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\{\mathcal N(\mu,\sigma^2),\mathcal N(\nu,\sigma^2)\}
 =\frac{(\mu-\nu)^2}{2\sigma^2}. \tag{8}
\]
The integrand in (8) vanishes outside \(B(x_j,h)\cup B(x_k,h)\).  The coordinate calculation in the witness-membership proof gives
\[
 \int_{B(x_j,h)}f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}(z)\,dz\le Ch^{\kappa},
\]
and the isolated polar calculation gives
\[
 \int_{B(x_{\star},h)}f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}(z)\,dz\le Ch^{\kappa}.
\]
Since \(0\le\psi_{j,h}\le1\), conditioning on \(X\) in (8), and summing the two coordinates if \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}\) denotes the full superpopulation law, therefore yields, in either family,
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h},\mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h})
 \le \frac{Ca^2h^{\kappa}}{\sigma^2}
 \le \frac{CL^2h^{\kappa+2}}{\sigma^2}. \tag{9}
\]
For product laws the log likelihood ratio is the sum of the coordinate log likelihood ratios.  Taking expectation and using (9) proves
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\otimes n},
 \mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h}^{\otimes n})
 \le \frac{CnL^2h^{\kappa+2}}{\sigma^2}. \tag{10}
\]

At an active center, \(\psi_{j,h}(x_j)=1\).  The trace formulas in \(\mathrm{def:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}family}\) now give
\[
 \theta_{1,P}(x_j)=\frac{Lh}{4},\qquad
 \theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-\frac{Lh}{4},\qquad
 \tau_P(x_j)=\frac{Lh}{2}.
\]
Together with (7) and (10), these are all the asserted properties.

Uniformly in \(x\in S^1\), the pervasive witness has \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides and \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp h^{-1}\). The isolated witness has \(q_{t,P}(x_{\star},h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides, a thin arc of length \(O(h)\), \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp1\), and the full upper profile in \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}profile\text{-}upper}\). Both witnesses have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).
semantic_closure.justification: The explicit circular laws prove nonemptiness and make the same-modulus, different-multiplicity comparison a legal within-model construction.

semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Write a point of the circular tube as
\[
 z=(1+s)(\cos\phi,\sin\phi),\qquad |s|\le h_0,quad 0\le\phi<2\pi .
\]
Because \(h_0<1\), these are nonsingular coordinates with area element \((1+s)\,ds\,d\phi\).  Hence the normalizing constant in \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\) is
\[
 Z_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 =2\pi\int_{-h_0}^{h_0}|s|^{\kappa-2}(1+s)\,ds
 =\frac{4\pi}{\kappa-1}h_0^{\kappa-1}.
\]
It is positive and finite, uniformly away from zero and infinity for \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\).  The isolated integrand is nonnegative, bounded by one, and positive off the single point \(x_{\star}\); compactness of \(\mathcal T\) and continuity in \(\kappa\in[2,\overline\kappa]\) therefore give the same uniform positivity and finiteness for its normalizer.

On a sufficiently small coordinate patch about any \(x\in S^1\), let \(s\) be signed normal depth and \(v\) signed arclength.  Compactness of \(S^1\), together with \(h_0<1\), supplies constants independent of \(x\) and \(\kappa\) for which the Jacobian is bounded above and below and
\[
 c(s^2+v^2)^{1/2}\le d(z,x)\le C(s^2+v^2)^{1/2}.
\]
Consequently, on either assignment side and for all sufficiently small \(h\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 q_{t,P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}}(x,h)
 &\asymp \int_0^h\int_{-\sqrt{h^2-s^2}}^{\sqrt{h^2-s^2}}
 s^{\kappa-2}\,dv\,ds\\
 &=h^{\kappa}\int_0^1 2w^{\kappa-2}\sqrt{1-w^2}\,dw
 \asymp h^{\kappa}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{1}
\]
The last integral is positive and is bounded above and below uniformly on the compact exponent interval.  By compactness and positivity, the constants can be enlarged so that (1) holds for every \(0<h\le h_0\).  Choose \(c_m>0\) below the uniform lower constant and \(C_m>c_m\) above the uniform upper constant.  Every boundary point then belongs to the thin set at level \(C_mh^{\kappa}\).  If \(E\) is a maximal \(h\)-separated subset of \(S^1\), the arcs of radius proportional to \(h\) about points of \(E\) are disjoint while arcs with twice that radius cover the circle.  Comparison with its arclength \(2\pi\) gives
\[
 c h^{-1}\le |E|\le C h^{-1}.
\]
Thus
\[
 \mathsf J_{P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}}(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp h^{-1}. \tag{2}
\]

For the isolated density put \(s_x=d(x,x_{\star})\).  The same coordinate comparison gives, uniformly in the side \(t\),
\[
 q_{t,P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(x,h)\ge
 \begin{cases}
 c h^{\kappa},&s_x\le2h,\\
 c h^2\min\{1,(s_x/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\},&s_x>2h.
 \end{cases} \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, in the first case one integrates the density over a side-specific subball of radius proportional to \(h\) whose distance from \(x_{\star}\) is proportional to \(h\); in the second case, on a subball of radius \(h/2\) about \(x\), the triangle inequality bounds the distance from \(x_{\star}\) below by a fixed multiple of \(s_x\).  Since \(s_x>2h\) in the second line and \(h_0<1\), both lines of (3) are bounded below by \(c'h^{\kappa}\).  At \(x=x_{\star}\), polar integration on either side also gives
\[
 q_{t,P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(x_{\star},h)
 \le C\int_0^h r^{\kappa-2}r\,dr
 \le C'h^{\kappa}. \tag{4}
\]
Equations (3)--(4) prove the common polynomial lower-mass condition and the asserted two-sided equivalence at \(x_{\star}\).

If \(a_{P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(x,h)\le u\), (3) implies
\[
 s_x\le C\left\{h+(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\right\}. \tag{5}
\]
An arc of the length on the right of (5) contains at most
\[
 C\left\{1+h^{-1}(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\right\}
\]
points separated by \(h\).  This is exactly \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}profile\text{-}upper}\), after enlarging \(C_{\mathrm{iso}}\).  At \(u=C_mh^{\kappa}\), (5) makes the upper bound constant, whereas (4) puts \(x_{\star}\) in the thin set.  Therefore
\[
 \mathsf J_{P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp1. \tag{6}
\]
All estimates extend to the remaining compact range of radii by changing constants.  The circle itself satisfies \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) by the same disjoint-arc and covering-arc calculation.  The exponent \(\kappa\) in (1) and (4) also agrees with the direct horn-volume calculation in \(\mathrm{lem:polynomial\text{-}horn\text{-}mass}\).

Finally, the assignment is sharp by the construction, the displayed potential-outcome formula implies consistency, and independence of the standard Gaussian variables gives \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\).  Both observed-side regressions and their traces are zero, hence satisfy \(\mathrm{ass:lipschitz\text{-}side\text{-}means}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}side\text{-}traces}\).  Equations (1)--(6), together with the class definitions, prove
\[
 P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},
 \qquad
 P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}.
\]
