semantic_closure.statement: Let \(Q_0,\ldots,Q_M\) be probability laws and let \(v_0,\ldots,v_M\) be elements of a metric space whose metric \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}\) satisfies \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(v_j,v_k)\ge 2\delta\) for \(j\ne k\). If \(M\ge2\) and \(M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)\le a\log M\), where \(0<a<1/8\), then every estimator \(\widehat v\) satisfies \(\max_{0\le j\le M}\mathbb E_{Q_j}\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_j)\ge c\delta\) for a numerical \(c>0\). If \(M=1\) and \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)\le1/8\), the same conclusion holds. These conclusions also hold for product experiments after replacing each \(Q_j\) by its product law.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
We give the information argument, so no unlisted testing theorem is being invoked. For the two-law assertion, any estimator induces the nearest-point test \(\widehat J\in\{0,1\}\). On \(\{\widehat J\ne j\}\), the triangle inequality gives \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_j)\ge\delta\). The smallest average testing error is
\[
 \frac12\int \min(dQ_0,dQ_1)=\frac{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)}2.
\]
For any measurable event \(A\), the log-sum inequality applied to the partition \(\{A,A^c\}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)
 \ge p\log\frac pq+(1-p)\log\frac{1-p}{1-q}
 \ge 2(p-q)^2,
\]
where \(p=Q_1(A)\) and \(q=Q_0(A)\). The last inequality follows by Taylor expansion in \(p\) around \(q\), since the second derivative is \(1/\{p(1-p)\}\ge4\). Taking the supremum over \(A\) proves \(\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\le\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)/2}\le1/4\). Hence the maximum risk is at least \(3\delta/8\).

For \(M\ge2\), let \(J\) be uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,M\}\), draw the observation from \(Q_J\), and put \(\overline Q=(M+1)^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^M Q_j\). The identity
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q)
 =\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,\overline Q)
 +(M+1)\operatorname{KL}(\overline Q,Q)
\]
follows by expanding the logarithms. With \(Q=Q_0\), it implies that the mutual information satisfies
\[
 I(J;Z)=\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,\overline Q)
 \le \frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=1}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)
 \le a\log M.
\]
For any decoder, if \(p_e=\Pr(\widehat J\ne J)\), conditioning on the error indicator gives
\[
 H(J\mid Z)\le \log2+p_e\log M.
\]
Since \(H(J)=\log(M+1)\), it follows that
\[
 p_e\ge\frac{\log(M+1)-a\log M-\log2}{\log M}.
\]
This is bounded below by a positive numerical constant for \(M\ge2\) after decreasing the harmless numerical restriction on \(a\) for the finitely many smallest \(M\). Nearest-point decoding again implies \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_J)\ge\delta\) on error. The displayed risk conclusion follows by averaging and then taking a maximum. The argument concerns only the laws supplied to it, so it applies verbatim to product laws.

semantic_closure.statement: For every fixed \(\alpha>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)>0\) for all \(h>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)\asymp h^{\alpha+1}\exp(-h^{-\alpha})\) as \(h\downarrow0\), and there exists \(h_n\downarrow0\) such that \(n m_{\alpha}(h_n)/\log n\to\infty\). Therefore a fixed exponential horn is compatible with logarithmically slow consistency and does not by itself force order-one risk.
semantic_closure.justification: This proposition removes a false early-kill premise before it contaminates the minimax theorem or the applied interpretation.
semantic_closure.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate obtains a logarithmic pointwise rate under severe design degeneracy; the present proposition records the corresponding boundary-modulus sanity condition without claiming a new minimax theorem.
semantic_closure.consumer: Applied analysts will not mistake an extremely thin but positive region for a formally non-estimable boundary segment.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Positivity is immediate from the strictly positive integrand in \(\mathrm{def:exponential\text{-}modulus}\). With the substitution \(s=u^{-\alpha}\),
\[
 m_\alpha(h)=\frac2\alpha\int_{h^{-\alpha}}^\infty e^{-s}s^{-1/\alpha-1}\,ds.
\]
Let \(a=1+1/\alpha\) and \(x=h^{-\alpha}\). Integration by parts gives
\[
 \int_x^\infty e^{-s}s^{-a}\,ds
 =e^{-x}x^{-a}-a\int_x^\infty e^{-s}s^{-a-1}\,ds.
\]
The last integral lies between zero and \(x^{-1}\int_x^\infty e^{-s}s^{-a}\,ds\). Consequently the ratio of the left side to \(e^{-x}x^{-a}\) is squeezed between \((1+a/x)^{-1}\) and one, and tends to one. Therefore
\[
 m_\alpha(h)\sim\frac2\alpha h^{\alpha+1}e^{-h^{-\alpha}}
 \qquad(h\downarrow0),
\]
which proves the claimed two-sided asymptotic order.

Choose \(h_n=(\tfrac12\log n)^{-1/\alpha}\) for large \(n\). Then \(h_n\downarrow0\), \(e^{-h_n^{-\alpha}}=n^{-1/2}\), and the asymptotic equivalence gives
\[
 \frac{n m_\alpha(h_n)}{\log n}
 \asymp n^{1/2}(\log n)^{-(\alpha+1)/\alpha-1}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Thus the fixed positive exponential modulus passes the effective-sample-size condition and cannot, by itself, imply an order-one lower bound.

In particular, the local-mass exponent is \(\kappa\), not \(\kappa-1\).

semantic_closure.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{def:polynomial\text{-}horn}\), a vertical section at inward coordinate \(u\) has length \(2u^{\kappa-1}\). Since \(B(0,h)\subset\{0<u<h\}\times[-h,h]\), direct integration of these nonnegative section lengths gives
\[
 \operatorname{Leb}_2(\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h))
 \le 2\int_0^h u^{\kappa-1}\,du=\frac{2}{\kappa}h^{\kappa}.
\]
For \(0<u<h/2\), one has \(h^2-u^2\ge3h^2/4\). Because \(\kappa>2\), for all sufficiently small \(h<h_0\), \(u^{\kappa-1}\le(h/2)^{\kappa-1}\le\sqrt3h/2\). Hence the entire section \(\{|v|\le u^{\kappa-1}\}\) lies in \(B(0,h)\), and therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Leb}_2(\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h))
 \ge2\int_0^{h/2}u^{\kappa-1}\,du
 =\frac{2^{1-\kappa}}{\kappa}h^{\kappa}.
\]
Taking \(c_\kappa=2^{1-\kappa}/\kappa\) and \(C_\kappa=2/\kappa\) proves both inequalities and shows that the exponent is \(\kappa\), rather than \(\kappa-1\).

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define
\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),\ 
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
In particular, uniformly over \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\), \(\mathbb E_P\sup_x W_n(x)\le C(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Moreover, for any \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
Thus the frozen assumptions yield an explicit honest global band and a computable two-law width obstruction. They do not by themselves establish the sharper uniform ratio to \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\): the global calibration uses \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), whereas \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\) can be bounded at an isolated thin site. Nor does the displayed two-law argument turn score-law total variation alone into an exact necessary-and-sufficient adaptation criterion without a same-class outcome perturbation whose full observed-law distance is controlled. This is a partial resolution of the honest-adaptation question.
proposed.justification: This theorem gives an exact-Gaussian finite-sample honest band with an explicit global calibration and a general full-observed-law two-law expected-width lower inequality.
proposed.gap: The local multiplicity benchmark can remove the global logarithm at isolated thin sites. The frozen premises do not yet prove that sharper width adaptation, its matching local-oracle ratio lower bound, or the requested score-law equivalence.
proposed.consumer: The Ser Pilo Paga replication can use the globally honest band immediately while treating local-oracle width adaptation as unresolved.

payload.tldr: The boundary target is the difference of the unique Lipschitz traces of the two observed-side regression classes on \(\operatorname{supp}(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t})\), so it is an observed-law functional even when conditional means at null boundary points are undefined. A single worst-point thickness modulus does not determine expected-sup difficulty: explicit circular designs with the same two-sided mass order \(h^{\kappa}\) have either one thin arc or \(\asymp h^{-1}\) separated thin sites, producing the matched rates \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) and \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\). A count-qualified estimator attains the pervasive rate without knowing \(\kappa\), and the arbitrary-modulus result gives an explicit global upper map and lower-profile testing bracket while proving that a lower packing declaration alone cannot recover the isolated frontier. Under the exact conditional Gaussian model, an explicit globally calibrated band has finite-sample simultaneous coverage and pervasive-rate expected supremum width, and every honest band obeys a full-observed-law two-law width obstruction. Local-oracle expected-width adaptation, its matching ratio lower bound, and an exact score-law distinguishability criterion remain open.

project_justification.fill: The project defines the target through unique Lipschitz representatives on restricted-score supports, constructs explicit symmetric circular witnesses and legal two-sided tent families, proves the same-modulus isolated--pervasive rate separation and a count-adaptive pervasive estimator, derives an arbitrary-modulus two-sided bracket with a lower-profile-only no-go certificate, and supplies an exact-Gaussian globally honest band plus a general full-law two-law width obstruction. The remaining inference frontier is the sharper local-oracle width problem and its score-design adaptation criterion.

sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling under a known sharp bivariate boundary assignment, with score density permitted to vanish at the boundary and exact conditionally Gaussian observed regression errors of fixed standard deviation \(\sigma\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Observed-side regressions are estimated by local constants with count-qualified bandwidths, a fixed measurable tie-break, and the explicit fallback \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)=h_0\) when no bandwidth is admissible. The settled band conditions on the scores and calibrates the finite disk-pattern family by the conditional sub-Gaussian bound derived from the exact Gaussian errors.

payload.related_work: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance is the causal and writing anchor: its Introduction motivates the full boundary curve, Theorem 4 derives the regular-density uniform stochastic term, Theorem 5 supplies Gaussian bands, and Theorem 6 gives a distance-estimator lower bound. Its density and Gram assumptions exclude the thinning regimes here, so it informs rather than supplies the proposed frontier. Gaiffas2005Degenerate, Theorems 1--2 and Section 3, motivates polynomial and severe design degeneracy in a one-dimensional pointwise model; it does not furnish the project-specific uniform two-sided boundary-mass condition, and its severe case shows that fixed exponential thinning permits logarithmically slow consistency. Gaiffas2007PointwiseAdaptive, Sections 2--4, supplies an empirical-design Lepski template at one query point. Gaiffas2007SharpSupNorm, its abstract and Section 1, constructs an unknown-design-density estimator with spatially varying sup-norm normalization and proposes an inhomogeneous confidence band, but assumes a positive continuous univariate density and supplies neither vanishing two-sided boundary mass nor a same-modulus multiplicity lower bound. Gaiffas2009Uniform, equation (2.1), Theorems 1--2, and Proposition 1, is the closest sup-loss regression comparator because it treats spatially varying rates and isolated density zeros, but it is univariate and does not provide a same-modulus two-sided boundary packing separation. AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 studies a different global-loss problem: Section 2 assumes a known univariate design density with finitely many well-separated polynomial or exponential zeros, Theorem 3.1 gives global \(L^2\) lower bounds, and Theorems 6.2 and 7.1 give adaptive upper bounds; it does not study a boundary-indexed sup loss, pervasive thin sites, or two assignment sides. Kpotufe2011LocalDimension uses observed neighbor radii for pointwise adaptation to local ball-mass growth. The displayed global boundary-entropy condition is project-specific: every covering step in the closed global upper bounds uses only its packing-number bound, not a local Ahlfors measure condition. ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2014Bands and ArmstrongKolesar2020Honest inform calibration and honest-width comparisons, but neither yields simultaneous local-oracle width under vanishing two-sided boundary information or converts score-law separation into the required full-experiment two-law obstruction. Bull2012SelfSimilarBands concerns unknown response smoothness rather than adaptation across observable score-design profiles.
payload.technical_internal_limitation: A scalar lower bound \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge m(h)\) cannot yield a sharp expected-sup converse without a compatible lower packing profile, and a lower packing declaration can be slack for upper-bound purposes. The proved arbitrary-modulus theorem therefore gives an honest two-sided bracket; the lower-profile-only no-go theorem shows that recovering the isolated frontier while retaining the pervasive subclass requires an upper thin-site restriction or an intrinsic two-sided profile. All closed estimator bounds use local constants under Lipschitz side regressions, avoiding unassumed local-polynomial Gram coercivity. For inference, the settled global band uses \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\); proving expected width proportional to \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\) requires a sharper local calibration. The available width obstruction is in total variation of the full observed experiments, and data processing does not permit it to be replaced by score-law total variation in the direction needed for a lower bound.
payload.honest_scope: The estimand is the identified contrast of unique Lipschitz observed-side traces on restricted-score supports, not a conditional expectation assigned directly at a probability-zero boundary point. The polynomial same-modulus thickness--multiplicity separation, its circular nonemptiness witnesses, the count-adaptive pervasive estimator, and the arbitrary-modulus two-sided bracket are settled. A lower mass modulus plus a lower packing declaration alone cannot encode the isolated frontier when the corresponding class retains pervasive laws; exact arbitrary-profile sharpness for a refined two-sided class remains open. For bands, the settled partial result is an explicit exact-Gaussian finite-sample globally honest construction, a pervasive expected-supremum width rate, and a general full-observed-law two-law width inequality. Uniform local-oracle expected width, its matching ratio lower bound, and the exact score-law distinguishability if-and-only-if remain open. The regular positive-density regime is an external benchmark on a different model class, not a reduction of the \(\kappa>2\) pervasive theorem.

payload.obstruction: The established band is calibrated over all realized disk patterns, so its stochastic radius contains \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\). At an isolated thin site, however, \(K_P(x,h)\) may remain bounded and the oracle logarithm \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\) is then of constant order. Thus the existing argument gives a diverging logarithmic ratio rather than a constant-factor upper bound. The established pervasive Fano converse controls \(\mathbb E_P[\sup_x W_n(x)]\), which does not imply a lower bound for \(\sup_x\mathbb E_P[W_n(x)]/r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\), and its packing scale is not a proof for arbitrary local benchmark functions. Finally, the general two-law inequality involves \(\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\) for full observed laws. Data processing only gives \(\operatorname{TV}(P_{0,X}^{\otimes n},P_{1,X}^{\otimes n})\le\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\), so it cannot replace the full-law distance by the score-law distance required by the proposed equivalence. No frozen assumption supplies local multiplicity calibration, uniformly consistent tests between all triangular profile components, or a relation reversing this inequality.
payload.attempted: First, the conditional sub-Gaussian disk-pattern union bound was localized by retaining only patterns near \(x\); without a proved local complexity or peeling lemma, simultaneous coverage still requires the global factor \(M_n\). Second, the pervasive tent family and the general two-law obstruction were specialized to a boundary point; the former yields only the established global expected-sup statement, while the latter yields a useful pointwise bound only after constructing two full laws with target separation on the oracle scale and controlled full-law total variation for every admissible profile. Third, a score-based selector followed by componentwise bands was considered. Pairwise score-law separation alone does not construct a uniform test over a possibly triangular and composite \(\Lambda_n\), and the frozen core provides neither a testing modulus nor compactness or cardinality control that would make this reduction necessary and sufficient.
payload.partial_result:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), put
\[
 M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj,
\]
and, with \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), define
\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
The established global-band theorem proves that the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and satisfies
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}
 P\!\left\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)
 \text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\right\}\ge 1-\gamma
\]
for every declared nonempty triangular union.  For every fixed admissible \(\kappa\) and fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), it also proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)\right]
 \le C_\gamma\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
When \(\gamma\) is smaller than one quarter of the universal numerical risk constant in the established finite-information testing lemma, every band honest over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)\right]
 \ge c_\gamma\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
The same lower bound holds for bands honest over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) whenever \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\).  Finally, without the small-\(\gamma\) restriction, every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge
 \frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]

proposed.statement:
Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), use the circular inside--outside assignment and constants certified by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), and suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\).  Put \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare
\[
 \mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=\mathbf 1\{u\ge C_mh^\kappa\},
 \qquad 0<h\le h_0,\quad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\cup
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}),
\]
and there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \le R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \le C\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 {r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The displayed inclusion and matched rate expose an internal limitation of the frozen arbitrary-modulus OEQ lower-profile-only exact-characterization demand for the two-argument class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\): matching same-class bounds cannot recover the isolated polynomial frontier when \(\mathsf J_{-}\) declares one thin site, because the class still retains the pervasive subclass. This is a limitation of that class parameterization, not a refutation of any published estimator or workflow. An arbitrary-modulus formulation that separates isolated from pervasive thinning must add an upper thin-site packing restriction or use an intrinsic two-sided profile.
proposed.justification: This theorem gives an explicit same-class polynomial witness for which a constant declared lower packing profile nevertheless has the pervasive logarithmic minimax rate.
proposed.gap: An exact arbitrary-modulus frontier for a refined class with upper as well as lower thin-site packing control remains unresolved; the frozen two-argument class cannot express the isolated side of that comparison.
proposed.consumer: The \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflow must not interpret a constant lower packing declaration as evidence of isolated thinning; it needs an upper-profile certificate before using an isolated-rate guarantee.

For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus N_{t,P}\), the residual \(\varepsilon_t=Y-g_{t,P}(X)\) is conditionally integrable and satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]=0,\qquad

and

payload.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\). By \(\mathrm{def:base\text{-}thickness\text{-}class}\), the law \(P\) satisfies \(\mathrm{ass:lipschitz\text{-}side\text{-}means}\), \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}side\text{-}traces}\), \(\mathrm{ass:polynomial\text{-}lower\text{-}mass}\), \(\mathrm{ass:sharp\text{-}assignment}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\). Write
\[
 \mu_t(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t),\qquad
 S_t=\operatorname{supp}(\mu_t)=\mathcal X_{t,P},\qquad
 \delta(z)=\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x),
\]
and let \(D_t=\{z\in S_t:\delta(z)<h_0\}\). The definition of \(g_{t,P}\) makes its restriction to \(D_t\) a Borel representative of the observed conditional-regression equivalence class, and \(\mathrm{ass:lipschitz\text{-}side\text{-}means}\) makes that restriction \(L\)-Lipschitz.

We first prove uniqueness on \(D_t\). Let \(f\) be any other \(L\)-Lipschitz representative there. Then \(f=g_{t,P}\) \(\mu_t\)-almost everywhere on \(D_t\). The complement of \(S_t\) is \(\mu_t\)-null: indeed, because \(\mathbb R^2\) has a countable base, that complement is a countable union of basis balls having \(\mu_t\)-measure zero by the definition of support. Suppose, toward a contradiction, that \(f(z_0)\ne g_{t,P}(z_0)\) at some \(z_0\in D_t\), and put \(\eta=|f(z_0)-g_{t,P}(z_0)|>0\). The distance function \(\delta\) is one-Lipschitz. Since \(L>0\), choose
\[
 0<r<\min\{h_0-\delta(z_0),\eta/(4L)\}.
\]
For every \(w\in S_t\) with \(d(w,z_0)<r\), one has \(w\in D_t\) and
\[
 |f(w)-g_{t,P}(w)|
 \ge \eta-|f(w)-f(z_0)|-|g_{t,P}(w)-g_{t,P}(z_0)|
 >\eta-2Lr>\eta/2.
\]
Because \(z_0\in S_t\), the ball \(B(z_0,r)\) has positive \(\mu_t\)-measure; because \(S_t^c\) is null, the displayed strict inequality holds on a set of positive \(\mu_t\)-measure. This contradicts equality of the two representatives almost everywhere. Hence \(g_{t,P}|_{D_t}\) is the unique \(L\)-Lipschitz representative.

Next fix \(x\in\mathcal B\). For every open neighborhood \(U\) of \(x\), choose \(0<h\le h_0\) so that \(\{z:d(z,x)\le h\}\subseteq U\). By \(\mathrm{ass:polynomial\text{-}lower\text{-}mass}\), the positivity of \(c_m\), and \(h>0\),
\[
 \mu_t(U)\ge q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge c_mh^\kappa>0.
\]
Thus \(x\in S_t\). In particular \(x\in D_t\), and, whenever \(z\in S_t\) tends to \(x\), the Lipschitz condition gives eventually
\[
 |g_{t,P}(z)-g_{t,P}(x)|\le Ld(z,x)\longrightarrow0.
\]
The trace in the definition of \(\theta_{t,P}\) therefore exists uniquely and equals \(g_{t,P}(x)\).

Now let \(P\) and \(Q\) be two laws in \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) inducing the same observed law of \(O=(Y,X)\). Their score marginals agree. Because the assignment geometry is known, their restricted measures \(E\mapsto P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t)\), supports \(S_t\), and observed conditional-regression equivalence classes also agree. The uniqueness just proved forces
\[
 g_{t,P}|_{D_t}=g_{t,Q}|_{D_t}.
\]
Taking the boundary limits gives \(\theta_{t,P}=\theta_{t,Q}\) on \(\mathcal B\), and subtracting the two side traces gives \(\tau_P=\tau_Q\). This proves the asserted observed-law identification without assigning an arbitrary conditional-mean version on the boundary.

It remains to verify the potential-outcome interpretation. Define the Borel set
\[
 C_t=\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}=t\}\cap\{z:\delta(z)<h_0\},
 \qquad p_t=P_X(C_t).
\]
If \(p_t=0\), the claimed almost-everywhere compatibility is vacuous. Suppose \(p_t>0\), and let \(P^{C_t}\) denote the law normalized to \(\{X\in C_t\}\). Since \(C_t\subseteq\mathcal A_t\), every \(\mu_t\)-null set is \(P_X\)-null after restriction to \(C_t\). Moreover \(P_X(C_t\setminus S_t)=0\). The corrected \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}regression\text{-}moments}\) therefore gives, for \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in C_t\),
\[
 \int y\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)=g_{t,P}(z),\qquad
 \int|y-g_{t,P}(z)|\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)\le\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}.
\]
For such a \(z\in C_t\cap S_t\), compactness of \(\mathcal B\) supplies \(x_z\in\mathcal B\) with \(d(z,x_z)=\delta(z)<h_0\). The trace equality already proved, \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}side\text{-}traces}\), and the Lipschitz condition yield
\[
 |g_{t,P}(z)|
 \le |g_{t,P}(x_z)|+Ld(z,x_z)
 =|\theta_{t,P}(x_z)|+Ld(z,x_z)
 \le L(1+h_0).
\]
Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1\{X\in C_t\}|Y|]
 \le p_t\{L(1+h_0)+\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}\}<\infty.
\]
On \(\{X\in C_t\}\), \(\mathrm{ass:sharp\text{-}assignment}\) gives \(T=t\) almost surely, and \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\) then gives \(Y=Y(t)\) almost surely. Thus \(Y(t)\) is integrable under \(P^{C_t}\). For every bounded Borel function \(\varphi\), the defining integral identity of the conditional kernel gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{P^{C_t}}[\varphi(X)Y(t)]
 &=p_t^{-1}\mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1\{X\in C_t\}\varphi(X)Y(t)]\\
 &=p_t^{-1}\mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1\{X\in C_t\}\varphi(X)Y]\\
 &=p_t^{-1}\int_{C_t}\varphi(z)g_{t,P}(z)\,P_X(dz)
 =\mathbb E_{P^{C_t}}[\varphi(X)g_{t,P}(X)].
\end{aligned}
\]
This integral characterization proves that the near-boundary representative is a version of the conditional mean of \(Y(t)\) under \(P^{C_t}\), almost everywhere under its score marginal. Finally, if \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), then
\[
 \mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}=t\}=\mathcal A_t
\]
for both \(t=0\) and \(t=1\). Hence the same compatibility holds \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\)-almost everywhere throughout the open \(h_0\)-tube, as claimed.

carrier.proof_tex:
The distance map \(z\mapsto d(z,x_j)\) is one-Lipschitz. Thus \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+\) is \(h^{-1}\)-Lipschitz, and each perturbed side regression in \(\mathrm{def:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}family}\) is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz. Its absolute trace is at most \(Lh/4\le L\) because \(0<h\le h_0/6<1\). The perturbation changes neither the score law nor any local-mass or packing property. The sharp-assignment and consistency properties follow directly from the construction.

For each Fano law \(P\) and side \(t\in\{0,1\}\), set
\[
 N_{t,P}=\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus\mathcal A_t.
\]
The set \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\) is closed by its definition as a support and
\(\mathcal A_t\) is Borel, so \(N_{t,P}\) is Borel.  Moreover, for the
one-sided restricted score measure,
\[
 \mu_{t,P}(N_{t,P})
 =P_X\bigl((\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus\mathcal A_t)
             \cap\mathcal A_t\bigr)=0. \tag{a}
\]
In the frozen circular construction,
\[
 \mathcal A_1=\{z:\rho(z)\le0\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_0=\{z:\rho(z)>0\}
 =\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1.
\]
Hence \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus N_{t,P}\) implies
\(z\in\mathcal A_t\), and the sharp assignment rule gives \(T(z)=t\).
Using the displayed tent formulas as Borel extensions off their
one-sided supports, a single regular conditional kernel for the
observed outcome is
\[
 \mathsf R_P(z,dy)
 =\mathcal N(g_{T(z),P}(z),\sigma^2)(dy).
\]
For every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus N_{t,P}\), this is
\(\mathcal N(g_{t,P}(z),\sigma^2)\).  Therefore
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}|y-g_{t,P}(z)|\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)<\infty,
 \qquad
 \int_{\mathbb R}\{y-g_{t,P}(z)\}\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)=0,
\]
and, for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}e^{\lambda\{y-g_{t,P}(z)\}}
 \,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)
 =e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}.
\]
Thus the integrability, centering, and moment-generating-function
requirements of \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\) hold with the
side-null sets in (a).  Boundary points assigned to the opposite side
are absorbed into \(N_{t,P}\).  The nullity calculation (a) itself does
not require overlap, while the implication \(T(z)=t\) here uses the
explicit complementary circular partition.  Consequently
\(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) and the class
definitions put every pervasive perturbation in
\(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and both isolated perturbations in
\(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\).

Maximality of the \(3h\)-separated set implies that arcs of radius \(3h\) cover \(S^1\), while arcs of radius \(3h/2\) about its points are disjoint. Comparing their total arclength with \(2\pi\) gives
\[
 c h^{-1}\le |\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\le C h^{-1}. \tag{7}
\]

Put \(a=Lh/4\). Conditional on \(X=z\), the relevant Gaussian coordinates under alternatives \(j\) and \(k\) have common variance \(\sigma^2\), and their mean difference has absolute value \(a|\psi_{j,h}(z)-\psi_{k,h}(z)|\). Direct integration of the Gaussian density gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\{\mathcal N(\mu,\sigma^2),\mathcal N(\nu,\sigma^2)\}
 =\frac{(\mu-\nu)^2}{2\sigma^2}. \tag{8}
\]
The integrand vanishes outside \(B(x_j,h)\cup B(x_k,h)\). The coordinate calculations in \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) give
\[
 \int_{B(x_j,h)}f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}(z)\,dz\le Ch^{\kappa},
 \qquad
 \int_{B(x_{\star},h)}f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}(z)\,dz\le Ch^{\kappa}.
\]
Since \(0\le\psi_{j,h}\le1\), conditioning on \(X\) in (8), and summing the two potential-outcome coordinates if the superpopulation experiment is used, gives in either family
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h},\mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h})
 \le \frac{Ca^2h^{\kappa}}{\sigma^2}
 \le \frac{CL^2h^{\kappa+2}}{\sigma^2}. \tag{9}
\]
The observed-data divergence is no larger, by marginalization. For the displayed product measures, likelihood ratios factor by the definition of a product law, so relative entropy is additive. Thus
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\otimes n},
 \mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h}^{\otimes n})
 \le \frac{CnL^2h^{\kappa+2}}{\sigma^2}. \tag{10}
\]
At an active center, \(\psi_{j,h}(x_j)=1\). The trace formulas in \(\mathrm{def:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}family}\) yield
\[
 \theta_{1,P}(x_j)=\frac{Lh}{4},\qquad
 \theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-\frac{Lh}{4},\qquad
 \tau_P(x_j)=\frac{Lh}{2}.
\]
Together with (7) and (10), these are all the asserted properties.

At an active site, their traces are \(\theta_{1,P}(x_j)=Lh/4\), \(\theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-Lh/4\), and \(\tau_P(x_j)=Lh/2\).

\]
The set \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\) is closed by its definition as a support and
\(\mathcal A_t\) is Borel, so \(N_{t,P}\) is Borel.  Moreover, for the
one-sided restricted score measure,
\[
 \mu_{t,P}(N_{t,P})
 =P_X\bigl((\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus\mathcal A_t)
             \cap\mathcal A_t\bigr)=0. \tag{a}
\]
In the frozen circular construction,
\[
 \mathcal A_1=\{z:\rho(z)\le0\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_0=\{z:\rho(z)>0\}
 =\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1.
\]
Hence \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus N_{t,P}\) implies
\(z\in\mathcal A_t\), and the sharp assignment rule gives \(T(z)=t\).
Using the displayed tent formulas as Borel extensions off their
one-sided supports, a single regular conditional kernel for the
observed outcome is
\[
 \mathsf R_P(z,dy)
 =\mathcal N(g_{T(z),P}(z),\sigma^2)(dy).
\]
For every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus N_{t,P}\), this is
\(\mathcal N(g_{t,P}(z),\sigma^2)\).  Therefore
\[

 \qquad
 \int_{\mathbb R}\{y-g_{t,P}(z)\}\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)=0,
\]
and, for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}e^{\lambda\{y-g_{t,P}(z)\}}
 \,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)
 =e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}.
\]
Thus the integrability, centering, and moment-generating-function
requirements of \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\) hold with the
side-null sets in (a).  Boundary points assigned to the opposite side
are absorbed into \(N_{t,P}\).  The nullity calculation (a) itself does
not require overlap, while the implication \(T(z)=t\) here uses the
explicit complementary circular partition.  Consequently
\(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) and the class
definitions put every pervasive perturbation in
\(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and both isolated perturbations in
\(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\).

 =\frac{(\mu-\nu)^2}{2\sigma^2}. \tag{8}

\[

\[

\[

 \theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-\frac{Lh}{4},\qquad

The isolated witness has \(q_{t,P}(x_{\star},h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides, a thin arc of length \(O(h)\), \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp1\), and the full upper profile in \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}profile\text{-}upper}\). semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Write a point of the circular tube as
\[
 z=(1+s)(\cos\phi,\sin\phi),\qquad |s|\le h_0,\quad 0\le\phi<2\pi.
\]
Because \(h_0<1\), these are nonsingular coordinates with area element \((1+s)\,ds\,d\phi\). Hence the pervasive normalizing constant from \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\) is
\[
 Z_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 =2\pi\int_{-h_0}^{h_0}|s|^{\kappa-2}(1+s)\,ds
 =\frac{4\pi}{\kappa-1}h_0^{\kappa-1}.
\]
It is positive and finite uniformly for \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\). The isolated integrand is nonnegative and bounded by one, so its normalizer is at most \(\operatorname{Leb}_2(\mathcal T)<\infty\). On the fixed positive-area subset \(\{z\in\mathcal T:d(z,x_{\star})\ge h_0/2\}\), it is at least \(2^{-(\overline\kappa-2)}\). Hence its normalizer is also bounded uniformly away from zero.

On a sufficiently small coordinate patch about any \(x\in S^1\), let \(s\) be signed normal depth and \(v\) signed arclength. Compactness of \(S^1\) and \(h_0<1\) give constants, uniform in \(x\) and \(\kappa\), for which the Jacobian is bounded above and below and
\[
 c(s^2+v^2)^{1/2}\le d(z,x)\le C(s^2+v^2)^{1/2}.
\]
Consequently, on either assignment side and for all sufficiently small \(h\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 q_{t,P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}}(x,h)
 &\asymp \int_0^h\int_{-\sqrt{h^2-s^2}}^{\sqrt{h^2-s^2}}
 s^{\kappa-2}\,dv\,ds\\
 &=h^{\kappa}\int_0^1 2w^{\kappa-2}\sqrt{1-w^2}\,dw
 \asymp h^{\kappa}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{1}
\]
The last integral is positive and bounded above and below uniformly on \([2,\overline\kappa]\). Compactness and positivity allow the constants to be enlarged so that (1) holds for every \(0<h\le h_0\). Choose \(c_m>0\) below the uniform lower constant and \(C_m>c_m\) above the uniform upper constant. Every boundary point then belongs to the thin set at level \(C_mh^{\kappa}\). If \(E\) is a maximal \(h\)-separated subset of \(S^1\), disjoint-arc and covering-arc comparisons with total arclength \(2\pi\) give
\[
 c h^{-1}\le |E|\le C h^{-1}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \mathsf J_{P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}}(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp h^{-1}. \tag{2}
\]

For the isolated density put \(s_x=d(x,x_{\star})\). The same coordinate comparison gives, uniformly in the side \(t\),
\[
 q_{t,P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(x,h)\ge
 \begin{cases}
 c h^{\kappa},&s_x\le2h,\\
 c h^2\min\{1,(s_x/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\},&s_x>2h.
 \end{cases} \tag{3}
\]
For the first line, integrate over a side-specific subball of radius proportional to \(h\) whose distance from \(x_{\star}\) is proportional to \(h\). For the second, use a subball of radius \(h/2\) about \(x\) and the triangle inequality. Since \(s_x>2h\) in the second line and \(h_0<1\), both lines are at least a uniform constant times \(h^{\kappa}\). At \(x=x_{\star}\), polar integration on either side also yields
\[
 q_{t,P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(x_{\star},h)
 \le C\int_0^h r^{\kappa-2}r\,dr
 \le C'h^{\kappa}. \tag{4}
\]
Equations (3)--(4) prove the common polynomial lower-mass condition and the asserted equivalence at \(x_{\star}\).

If \(a_{P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(x,h)\le u\), equation (3) implies, after enlarging a uniform constant to cover the case in which the right-hand side exceeds the circle's diameter,
\[
 s_x\le C\left\{h+(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\right\}. \tag{5}
\]
An arc of the length on the right-hand side of (5) contains at most
\[
 C\left\{1+h^{-1}(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\right\}
\]
points separated by \(h\). This is \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}profile\text{-}upper}\), after enlarging \(C_{\mathrm{iso}}\). At \(u=C_mh^{\kappa}\), this upper bound is constant, while (4) puts \(x_{\star}\) in the thin set. Hence
\[
 \mathsf J_{P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp1. \tag{6}
\]
The estimates extend to the remaining compact range of radii by changing constants. The circle satisfies \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) by the same arc argument. The exponent in (1) and (4) also agrees with \(\mathrm{lem:polynomial\text{-}horn\text{-}mass}\).

Finally, the assignment is sharp by construction and the displayed observed-outcome equation gives consistency. For either witness the kernel
\[
 \mathsf R_P(z,dy)=\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)(dy)
\]
is a single regular conditional law of observed \(Y\) given \(X=z\). On each side, \(g_{t,P}(z)=0\), so for every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), and with the empty null set,
\[
 \int |y-g_{t,P}(z)|\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)<\infty,
 \quad
 \int \{y-g_{t,P}(z)\}\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)=0,
 \quad
 \int e^{\lambda\{y-g_{t,P}(z)\}}\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)
 =e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}.
\]
Thus the corrected observed-side condition \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\) holds exactly. Both observed-side regressions and traces are zero, so the Lipschitz and trace-envelope properties hold. Equations (1)--(6) and the class definitions prove
\[
 P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},
 \qquad
 P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}.
\]

semantic_closure.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{def:polynomial\text{-}horn}\), a vertical section of \(\mathsf H_{\kappa}\) at inward coordinate \(u\) has length \(2u^{\kappa-1}\). Since \(B(0,h)\subset\{0<u<h\}\times[-h,h]\), Tonelli's theorem for the nonnegative section indicator gives
\[
 \operatorname{Leb}_2\{\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h)\}
 \le 2\int_0^h u^{\kappa-1}\,du
 =\frac{2}{\kappa}h^{\kappa}.
\]
For \(0<u<h/2\), one has \(h^2-u^2\ge3h^2/4\). Because \(\kappa>2\), for all sufficiently small \(h<h_0\),
\[
 u^{\kappa-1}\le(h/2)^{\kappa-1}\le \sqrt{3}h/2.
\]
Hence the entire section \(\{|v|\le u^{\kappa-1}\}\) lies in \(B(0,h)\), and another application of Tonelli gives
\[
 \operatorname{Leb}_2\{\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h)\}
 \ge 2\int_0^{h/2}u^{\kappa-1}\,du
 =\frac{2^{1-\kappa}}{\kappa}h^{\kappa}.
\]
Thus one may take \(c_{\kappa}=2^{1-\kappa}/\kappa\) and \(C_{\kappa}=2/\kappa\). Both are positive and finite, and the power is \(\kappa\), not \(\kappa-1\).

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), fix an assignment geometry satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\), and suppose \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\). For every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), every sequence \(\epsilon_n\downarrow0\), and every data-measurable band sequence satisfying
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}
 \ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n,
\]
there is \(c_\gamma>0\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \ge c_\gamma r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 \frac{\mathbb E_PW_n(x)}{r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)}
 \ge c_\gamma.
\]
Every band honest over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) obeys the first conclusion, and it obeys the second conclusion whenever widths are compared over its pervasive subclass. These conclusions hold for every such assignment geometry; the circular laws are needed only as explicit nonemptiness witnesses.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Choose an arbitrary \(P^\circ\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), whose existence is the stated nonemptiness premise, and retain its score marginal \(P_X^\circ\) and assignment geometry. On an extension carrying independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), define \(Q_0\) by \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\) and by the consistency equation for the observed outcome. The sharp-assignment and consistency conditions hold by construction. The boundary entropy, polynomial lower mass, and pervasive packing conditions depend only on the retained score law and geometry. Both side regressions and traces are zero, so the Lipschitz and bounded-trace conditions hold, and the single observed-outcome kernel is exactly centered Gaussian with variance \(\sigma^2\). Hence every member condition in \(\mathrm{def:base\text{-}thickness\text{-}class}\) and \(\mathrm{def:pervasive\text{-}thinning\text{-}class}\) holds, and
\[
 Q_0\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}. \tag{77}
\]

Put \(r_n=(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), fix \(a_\gamma=(1-\gamma)/4\), and let \(h=b_\gamma r_n\), where the fixed constant \(b_\gamma>0\) will be chosen below. For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(h\le h_0\). The pervasive thin-site condition and the definition of \(\mathsf J_{Q_0}\) provide an \(h\)-separated set \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_M\}\subseteq\mathcal B\) with
\[
 M\ge\lfloor c_Jh^{-1}\rfloor,
 \qquad
 a_{Q_0}(x_j,h)\le C_mh^\kappa. \tag{78}
\]
For each \(j\), choose \(t_j\in\{0,1\}\) attaining the minimum in \(a_{Q_0}(x_j,h)\), so that
\[
 q_{t_j,Q_0}(x_j,h)\le C_mh^\kappa. \tag{79}
\]
Set \(\eta=\min\{L/6,1\}\), \(\Delta=\eta h\), and
\[
 \phi_j(z)=\left(1-\frac{3d(z,x_j)}h\right)_+.
\]
For \(j\ge1\), retain the score law and independent Gaussian noises and define \(Q_j\) by
\[
 \begin{cases}
 Y(1)=\Delta\phi_j(X)+\sigma Z_1,\quad Y(0)=\sigma Z_0,&t_j=1,\\
 Y(1)=\sigma Z_1,\quad Y(0)=-\Delta\phi_j(X)+\sigma Z_0,&t_j=0.
 \end{cases} \tag{80}
\]
The perturbed side mean in (80) is \(3\eta\)-Lipschitz, and \(3\eta\le L/2<L\). Also \(0<h\le h_0<1\) implies \(\Delta\le\eta\le L/6<L\). Thus the Lipschitz and bounded-trace conditions hold. All score-dependent conditions are unchanged and, after subtracting the appropriate side mean, the single observed-outcome kernel gives a \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) residual on each restricted side. The same member-by-member verification as in (77) therefore proves
\[
 Q_j\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},\qquad 0\le j\le M. \tag{81}
\]
This membership conclusion is derived from the frozen class conditions and does not use the circular tent family.

The supports of the tents have radius \(h/3\), whereas the centers are \(h\)-separated. Consequently, for \(j\ne k\), \(\phi_j(x_k)=0\), while \(\phi_j(x_j)=1\). Continuity of the Lipschitz side means gives their boundary traces, so
\[
 \tau_{Q_0}(x_k)=0,
 \qquad
 \tau_{Q_j}(x_k)=\Delta\mathbf 1\{j=k\}. \tag{82}
\]
Only observations in \(\mathcal A_{t_j}\cap B(x_j,h/3)\) have a shifted observed conditional mean under \(Q_j\). The conditional Gaussian likelihood formula, (79), and \(0\le\phi_j\le1\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_j^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 &=\frac{n\Delta^2}{2\sigma^2}
   \int_{\mathcal A_{t_j}}\phi_j(z)^2\,dP_X^\circ(z)\\
 &\le\frac{n\eta^2h^2}{2\sigma^2}q_{t_j,Q_0}(x_j,h)
 \le \frac{C_m\eta^2}{2\sigma^2}nh^{\kappa+2}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{83}
\]
Independent sampling justifies both the product experiment and the additive product-law divergence in (83).

Since \(nh^{\kappa+2}=b_\gamma^{\kappa+2}\log n\), while (78) implies
\[
 \log M\ge \frac{1}{2(\kappa+2)}\log n \tag{84}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), one may choose \(b_\gamma>0\), depending on \(\gamma\) and the fixed class envelopes but not on \(n\), so that
\[
 \frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_j^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le a_\gamma\log M. \tag{85}
\]
The explicit entropy-decoding inequality \(\mathrm{lem:explicit\text{-}entropy\text{-}decoding\text{-}bound}\) now yields, for every decoder \(\widehat J\),
\[
 \frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M Q_j^{\otimes n}\{\widehat J\ne j\}
 \ge p_n:=\frac{\log(M+1)-a_\gamma\log M-\log2}{\log M}. \tag{86}
\]
Because \(M\to\infty\),
\[
 p_n\longrightarrow1-a_\gamma=\frac{3+\gamma}{4}>\gamma. \tag{87}
\]
In particular, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(p_n-\gamma-\epsilon_n\ge(1-\gamma)/2\).

We first obtain the global-width conclusion. Put \(W_n^*=\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)\). From the reported intervals at \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\), let \(\widehat J\) be the smallest code index \(j\in\{0,\ldots,M\}\) for which the vector \((\tau_{Q_j}(x_1),\ldots,\tau_{Q_j}(x_M))\) lies in their Cartesian product, using zero if no index qualifies. On the simultaneous-coverage event under \(Q_j\), code \(j\) qualifies. If additionally \(W_n^*<\Delta/2\), no two codes qualify, because (82) makes two distinct codes differ by \(\Delta\) in some coordinate, whereas every reported interval has diameter less than \(\Delta\). Therefore Markov's inequality gives
\[
 Q_j^{\otimes n}\{\widehat J\ne j\}
 \le\gamma+\epsilon_n+
 \frac{2\mathbb E_{Q_j}W_n^*}{\Delta}. \tag{88}
\]
If one of these expectations is infinite, the desired bound is immediate. Otherwise, average (88), use (86)--(87), and obtain
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \ge\frac{\Delta}{2}(p_n-\gamma-\epsilon_n)
 \ge\frac{\eta b_\gamma(1-\gamma)}4 r_n. \tag{89}
\]
This proves the first conclusion with a constant depending on \(\gamma\), never on \(n\).

For the pointwise conclusion, define another decoder to equal zero if every \(\mathcal C_n(x_k)\) contains zero, and otherwise to equal the smallest \(k\) for which zero is absent. Under \(Q_0\), simultaneous coverage implies correct decoding. Under \(Q_j\), equation (82), simultaneous coverage, and \(W_n(x_j)<\Delta/2\) imply that every inactive interval contains zero while the active interval contains \(\Delta\) and excludes zero. Hence
\[
 Q_0^{\otimes n}\{\widehat J\ne0\}\le\gamma+\epsilon_n,
 \qquad
 Q_j^{\otimes n}\{\widehat J\ne j\}
 \le\gamma+\epsilon_n+\frac{2\mathbb E_{Q_j}W_n(x_j)}\Delta. \tag{90}
\]
Average (90), compare with (86), and use (87). For at least one \(j\ge1\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q_j}W_n(x_j)
 \ge \frac{M+1}{2M}\Delta(p_n-\gamma-\epsilon_n)
 \ge c_\gamma r_n. \tag{91}
\]

It remains to compare (91) to the declared local benchmark. For all sufficiently large \(n\), the dyadic grid contains \(\overline h\) with \(h\le\overline h<2h\). Polynomial lower mass, retained by every \(Q_j\), gives
\[
 q_{t,Q_j}(x_j,\overline h)\ge c_m\overline h^\kappa,
 \qquad t\in\{0,1\}. \tag{92}
\]
Every \(\overline h\)-separated set counted by \(\mathsf J_{Q_j}(\overline h,a_{Q_j}(x_j,\overline h))\) is an \(\overline h\)-separated subset of the whole boundary. Global boundary entropy and \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}effective\text{-}multiplicity}\) therefore imply
\[
 K_{Q_j}(x_j,\overline h)\le1\vee C_{\mathcal B}\overline h^{-1}. \tag{93}
\]
Insert \(\overline h\) into the infimum in \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}oracle\text{-}benchmark}\). Equations (92)--(93), \(\overline h\asymp r_n\), and \(nr_n^{\kappa+2}=\log n\) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 r_{n,Q_j}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x_j)
 &\le2L\overline h+
 \sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log\{e(1\vee C_{\mathcal B}\overline h^{-1})/\gamma\}}n
 \left\{q_{0,Q_j}(x_j,\overline h)^{-1}
       +q_{1,Q_j}(x_j,\overline h)^{-1}\right\}}\\
 &\le C_\gamma r_n.
 \end{aligned} \tag{94}
\]
Combining (91) and (94) proves the pointwise ratio bound.

Finally, \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) by definition. A band honest over the base class is therefore honest over the pervasive subclass, and the supremum over the base class is no smaller. Thus (89) transfers to the base class. No step used circular geometry; the only geometric facts used were the frozen pervasive packing lower bound and global boundary packing upper bound.

semantic_closure.citation: Cattaneo, M. D., R. Titiunik, and R. R. Yu (2026). Estimation and Inference in Boundary Discontinuity Designs: Distance-Based Methods. Journal of Econometrics 256, 106266; arXiv:2510.26051.
Hahn, J., P. Todd, and W. van der Klaauw (2001). Identification and Estimation of Treatment Effects with a Regression-Discontinuity Design. Econometrica 69, 201--209.

semantic_closure.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and \(m(r)>0\) for every \(0<r\le h_0\). For every nonempty class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\), let \(\overline\tau_n(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\widehat\tau_n(x)\}\), where \(\Pi_I\) is Euclidean projection onto the interval \(I\). There are constants \(A,C,c,a>0\), depending only on the fixed envelopes, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\min\left[ L,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\\nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)}}
 \left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}\right],
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). The estimator in this display uses neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\); they occur only in its guarantee. Conversely, if \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\), then
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh
\]
whenever either \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), or \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\). Hence a sufficient uniform-consistency condition for a sequence of nonempty such classes with lower moduli \(m_n\) is the existence of \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\); a necessary condition is that the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible values of \(h\) in the preceding display tends to zero. For a fixed positive exponential modulus \(m_\alpha\), the sufficient condition holds. With polynomial profiles, the lower display yields the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp1\) and the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp h^{-1}\); together with \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), these rates are exact. For an arbitrary slack lower packing declaration, the lower display need not match the upper display based on global boundary entropy, so this is a proved two-sided bracket, not an assertion of an unproved exact arbitrary-profile criterion.
semantic_closure.justification: This theorem gives an explicit count-based global upper map and a legal same-class Lipschitz-tent converse indexed by the declared lower packing profile.
semantic_closure.gap: The two sides match in the isolated and pervasive polynomial regimes. For arbitrary declarations they can differ because \(\mathsf J_{-}\) may be slack while the upper argument covers the full boundary using global entropy.
semantic_closure.consumer: The \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflow can check the sufficient count condition before fitting and report a lower testing experiment when uniform consistency is impossible.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\), and write \(\mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t)\). If \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(r>0\), and \(s=\min\{h_0,r/2\}\), positivity of \(m\) and the declared lower-mass member property in \(\mathrm{def:modulus\text{-}profile\text{-}class}\) give
\[
 \mu_{t,P}\{z:d(z,x)<r\}\ge q_{t,P}(x,s)\ge m(s)>0. \tag{49}
\]
Thus \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) on both sides. The Lipschitz member property makes the specified representative \(g_{t,P}\) continuous at \(x\), so the definition of the boundary trace gives
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x). \tag{50}
\]
The complementary assignment and the definition of \(T\) identify each side average with observations having \(T=t\). The bounded-trace member property gives \(\tau_P(x)\in[-2L,2L]\). Since Euclidean projection onto a closed interval containing the target is nonexpansive, projection cannot increase the pointwise error, and its pointwise loss is at most \(4L\).

For the upper bound, fix \(h\) such that \(h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\) and
\[
 nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h). \tag{51}
\]
Let \(z_1,\ldots,z_K\) be a maximal \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\). Maximality makes it an \(h\)-net, while \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) gives \(K\le C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}\). By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), \(\mathrm{def:empirical\text{-}counts}\), and the lower-mass member property,
\[
 N_{t,n}(z_j,h)\sim\operatorname{Bin}\{n,q_{t,P}(z_j,h)\},
 \qquad q_{t,P}(z_j,h)\ge m(h). \tag{52}
\]
For \(N\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), Markov's inequality applied to \(2^{-N}\), followed by \(1-y\le e^{-y}\), yields
\[
 \Pr(N\le nq/2)
 \le 2^{nq/2}\mathbb E(2^{-N})
 =2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n
 \le e^{-nq(1-\log 2)/2}
 \le e^{-nq/8}. \tag{53}
\]
Let \(H_h\) be the event that every center-side count is at least \(nm(h)/2\). A union bound over the \(2K\) pairs in (52) gives
\[
 P(H_h^c)\le2C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}. \tag{54}
\]
For each \(x\in\mathcal B\), choose a net center \(z_j\) with \(d(x,z_j)\le h\). The triangle inequality gives \(B(z_j,h)\subseteq B(x,2h)\), and hence, on \(H_h\),
\[
 \inf_{x\in\mathcal B,\,t\in\{0,1\}}N_{t,n}(x,2h)\ge nm(h)/2. \tag{55}
\]
Choose the fixed constant \(A\ge16\). Equations (51) and (55), together with \(\log(e+n/(2h))\le\log(e+n/h)\), show that \(2h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\) for every \(x,t\) on \(H_h\).

Condition on \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\). The selected bandwidths are then fixed functions of the scores. By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), the conditional law is the product of the single observed-outcome kernels. For an index on side \(t\), the corrected restricted-side clause of \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\) applies to \(Y_i-g_{t,P}(X_i)\). Consequently, for every deterministic index set \(S\) belonging to one side,
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \exp\!\left\{\lambda\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i\right\}
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 \le \exp\{\sigma^2\lambda^2|S|/2\}. \tag{56}
\]
Thus the disk-pattern count and conditional tail calculation in \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\) apply. If \(Z_n\) denotes the maximum normalized residual sum appearing there, then
\[
 \mathbb E_P(Z_n\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)
 \le\sqrt{2\log\!\left\{4|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\right\}}+1
 \le C_0\sqrt{\log(e+n)}. \tag{57}
\]
For a nonempty side average at bandwidth \(b\), equation (50) and the Lipschitz member property give conditional bias at most \(Lb\). Its stochastic error is at most \(\sigma Z_n/\sqrt{N_{t,n}(x,b)}\). Since \(b\le h_0<1\) implies \(\log(e+n/b)\ge\log(e+n)\), equation (57) bounds the conditional expected stochastic error uniformly by a constant times the stochastic term in the selection criterion. On \(H_h\), the selected set is nonempty and pointwise minimization of that criterion, followed by comparison with the admissible bandwidth \(2h\) from (55), gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 \le C_1\left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}. \tag{58}
\]
Here the factor two from the two sides is absorbed into \(C_1\).

Projection, the \(4L\) loss bound on \(H_h^c\), and (54) now yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\\
 &\quad\le C_2\left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}
 +C_3Lh^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{59}
\]
After increasing \(A\) so that \(A/8\ge2\), equation (51) implies
\[
 h^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}
 \le h^{-1}(e+n/h)^{-2}
 \le h,
\]
so the final term in (59) is absorbed into the bias term. Taking the infimum over qualifying dyadic pairs and combining with the unconditional \(4L\) bound proves the upper display. The definitions of the empirical counts, admissible bandwidths, count-adaptive bandwidth, estimator, and fixed projection show directly that this single data-driven estimator uses neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\).

We next prove the same-class converse. Choose \(P^\circ\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\), which exists by the theorem's nonemptiness premise, and retain its score marginal and assignment geometry. On an extension carrying independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), define \(P_0\) by \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\) and define the observed outcome by consistency. All score-dependent member properties are unchanged, both side regressions and traces vanish, and the single observed-outcome kernel is exactly centered Gaussian with variance \(\sigma^2\). Thus all member conditions in \(\mathrm{def:modulus\text{-}profile\text{-}class}\) hold and \(P_0\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\).

Fix \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and put \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\ge1\). The declared-profile member property and the definition of \(\mathsf J_{P_0}\) supply \(h\)-separated points \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) such that \(a_{P_0}(x_j,h)\le u\). For every \(j\), choose \(t_j\in\{0,1\}\) with \(q_{t_j,P_0}(x_j,h)\le u\), and set
\[
 \eta_h=\frac{Lh}{12},
 \qquad
 \psi_{j,h}(z)=\left(1-\frac{3d(z,x_j)}h\right)_+. \tag{60}
\]
Define \(P_j\) by retaining the score law and independent Gaussian noises and setting
\[
 \begin{cases}
 Y(1)=\eta_h\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_1,\quad Y(0)=\sigma Z_0,&t_j=1,\\
 Y(1)=\sigma Z_1,\quad Y(0)=-\eta_h\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_0,&t_j=0.
 \end{cases} \tag{61}
\]
The perturbation in (61) is \(3\eta_h/h=L/4\)-Lipschitz. Since \(h\le h_0/3<1\), its absolute trace is at most \(\eta_h<L\). It changes neither the score-dependent conditions nor the centered Gaussian observed residual kernel. Therefore every \(P_j\) belongs to \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\); this derives membership from the class conditions rather than assigning it by construction.

At \(x_j\), the target under \(P_j\) equals \(\eta_h\). If \(k\ne j\), the \(h\)-separation of the centers and the radius-\(h/3\) support of the tents imply \(\psi_{k,h}(x_j)=0\). Consequently,
\[
 \|\tau_{P_j}-\tau_{P_k}\|_\infty\ge\eta_h,
 \qquad 0\le j<k\le M. \tag{62}
\]
Only observations with \(X\in\mathcal A_{t_j}\cap B(x_j,h/3)\) have a shifted observed conditional mean. The exact centered-Gaussian likelihood formula and \(0\le\psi_{j,h}\le1\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 &=\frac{n\eta_h^2}{2\sigma^2}
   \int_{\mathcal A_{t_j}}\psi_{j,h}(z)^2\,dP_X(z)\\
 &\le\frac{nL^2h^2}{288\sigma^2}
   q_{t_j,P_0}(x_j,h)
 \le\frac{nL^2h^2u}{288\sigma^2}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{63}
\]
If \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), retain one alternative and choose the universal \(a>0\) so that (63) is at most \(1/8\). The two-law clause of \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), applied with \(2\delta=\eta_h\), yields minimax risk at least \(cLh\). If instead \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\), use \(\log(M+1)/\log M\le\log3/\log2\) and decrease \(a\) by that universal factor. Then (63) meets the multiple-law hypothesis of the same lemma, and (62) yields
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh. \tag{64}
\]

For a sequence of nonempty classes with moduli \(m_n\), the displayed sufficient condition supplies qualifying \(h_n\) eventually; equation (59) then tends to zero because \(h_n\downarrow0\) and \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\). Conversely, let \(F_n\) be the set of radii for which some \(u\) satisfies either information condition in the lower display. If \(\sup F_n\not\to0\), then along a subsequence there are feasible radii bounded below by a positive constant, and (64) keeps the minimax risk bounded away from zero. This proves the stated necessary condition.

For \(m_\alpha\), \(\mathrm{prop:exponential\text{-}horn\text{-}consistency}\) gives \(m_\alpha(h)\asymp h^{\alpha+1}e^{-h^{-\alpha}}\). Set \(s_n=\{(\log n)/2\}^{-1/\alpha}\). Then
\[
 \frac{nm_\alpha(s_n)}{\log(e+n/s_n)}
 \asymp\frac{n^{1/2}s_n^{\alpha+1}}{\log n}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{65}
\]
Round upward to a dyadic \(h_n\in\mathcal H_n\) with \(s_n\le h_n<2s_n\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), this point is not a grid endpoint, so \(2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\); monotonicity of \(m_\alpha\) and \(h_n<2s_n\) preserve (65). Hence the sufficient condition holds for every fixed positive exponential modulus.

Finally, put \(u=C_mh^\kappa\). When \(M\asymp1\), the first information condition balances \(nh^{\kappa+2}\asymp1\), and therefore gives \(h\asymp n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\). When \(M\asymp h^{-1}\), the second balances \(nh^{\kappa+2}\asymp\log(1/h)\), and therefore gives \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\). These lower rates match the two rates in \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\). For a slack declaration, the circular pervasive witness can be paired with \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=\mathbf1\{u\ge C_mh^\kappa\}\): the declared lower profile then exposes only one site, whereas the global-net upper argument still pays for the full boundary entropy. Thus the arbitrary-profile result is the claimed two-sided bracket and does not assert an unproved exact criterion.

semantic_closure.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define
\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
Fix an admissible \(\kappa\).  For every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), there is \(C_\gamma<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \le C_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\). For any admissible assignment geometry under the preceding premises, whenever \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\), for every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\) and every sequence \(\epsilon_n\downarrow0\), there is \(c_\gamma>0\), independent of \(n\), such that every data-measurable band sequence satisfying
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}
 \ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n
\]
obeys, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \ge c_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)},
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 \frac{\mathbb E_PW_n(x)}{r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)}
 \ge c_\gamma.
\]
Every band honest over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) obeys the global lower bound because \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\), and it obeys the ratio conclusion when widths are compared over its pervasive subclass. The circular witnesses in \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) certify explicit nonemptiness only. Thus, whenever the pervasive class is nonempty, the displayed band attains the matched global expected-sup half-width frontier on the pervasive and base classes.

Independently of the preceding pervasive-class conclusions, for any \(\gamma\in(0,1)\) and \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
Uniform local-oracle width achievability over an arbitrary triangular union, the corresponding local-ratio converse for unions without a nonempty pervasive component, and an exact necessary-and-sufficient criterion stated only through score-law total variation remain open. The global calibration uses \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), whereas \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\) can remain bounded at an isolated thin site, and score-law total variation alone does not control the distance between full observed laws.
semantic_closure.justification: Conditional sub-Gaussian disk-pattern calibration gives finite-sample simultaneous coverage for arbitrary declared complementary geometries. The geometry-general disjoint-tent construction supplies, at every fixed miscoverage level, both the matched global expected-supremum half-width converse and the local-benchmark ratio converse on every nonempty pervasive component; circular witnesses certify explicit nonemptiness only.

semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Let \(P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\). By \(\mathrm{def:triangular\text{-}profile\text{-}union}\), \(P\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) for at least one \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), and hence it satisfies every member condition in \(\mathrm{def:base\text{-}thickness\text{-}class}\). We first verify the trace relation used by the band. Fix \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(s>0\), and put \(b=\min\{h_0,s/2\}\). The polynomial lower-mass member property gives
\[
 P_X\{z\in\mathcal A_t:d(z,x)<s\}
 \ge q_{t,P}(x,b)\ge c_m b^\kappa>0. \tag{95}
\]
Thus every neighborhood of \(x\) has positive mass under the one-sided restricted score measure, so \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\). The Lipschitz condition \(\mathrm{ass:lipschitz\text{-}side\text{-}means}\) makes \(g_{t,P}\) continuous at \(x\) on \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\). Consequently, the definition of the boundary trace yields
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x). \tag{96}
\]

Write
\[
 z_n=\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)}.
\]
For fixed scores, denote by \(\mathscr S_n\) the disk-pattern family in \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\). Its cardinality is at most \(M_n\). Substitution of \(z_n\) into that lemma gives, for \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-almost every score vector,
\[
 \Pr_P\!\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{\left|\sum_{i\in S}\{Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\}\right|}
 {\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z_n
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le 2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z_n^2/2}\le\gamma. \tag{97}
\]
Here \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and the corrected \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\) are exactly the sampling and single-kernel restricted-side MGF premises of the established lemma. Complementarity \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and the definition of \(T\) ensure that a side-\(t\) disk pattern contains exactly observations with \(T_i=t\).

Consider the selected side fit at \((x,t)\), and abbreviate
\[
 \widehat h=\widehat h_{t,n}(x),\qquad
 N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h),\qquad
 S=\{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le\widehat h\}.
\]
If \(N>0\), then \(S\in\mathscr S_n\), and on the event complementary to that in (97),
\[
 \left|\frac1N\sum_{i\in S}\{Y_i-g_{t,P}(X_i)\}\right|
 \le \sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)}{N}}. \tag{98}
\]
Moreover, (96) and \(\mathrm{ass:lipschitz\text{-}side\text{-}means}\) imply
\[
 \left|\frac1N\sum_{i\in S}g_{t,P}(X_i)-\theta_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \le \frac1N\sum_{i\in S}L\,d(X_i,x)\le L\widehat h. \tag{99}
\]
Equations (98)--(99) and \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}constant\text{-}side\text{-}fit}\) show that the side error is at most \(B_{t,n}(x)\). If \(N=0\), that definition makes the side fit equal to zero, while \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}side\text{-}traces}\) gives
\[
 |\widehat g_{t,n}(x;\widehat h)-\theta_{t,P}(x)|\le L=B_{t,n}(x). \tag{100}
\]
Because (97) controls every disk pattern simultaneously, (98)--(100) hold simultaneously for all \(x\in\mathcal B\) and both sides with conditional probability at least \(1-\gamma\). Using \(\mathrm{def:mass\text{-}adaptive\text{-}estimator}\) and the definition \(\tau_P=\theta_{1,P}-\theta_{0,P}\), the triangle inequality gives
\[
 |\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\le B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\qquad(x\in\mathcal B). \tag{101}
\]
Thus the displayed band contains \(\tau_P(x)\) for every \(x\) on this event. Integrating (97) over the scores proves
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}
 P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma. \tag{102}
\]
For measurability, each count and numerator is a finite sum of Borel functions of the data and \(x\); \(\mathcal H_n\) is finite; and \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\) specifies both a deterministic tie break and an empty-set value. Hence \(\widehat h_{t,n}\), the selected fits, the radii \(B_{t,n}\), and the two interval endpoints are data measurable.

We next prove the expected-width upper bound. Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), put
\[
 r_n=\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}, \tag{103}
\]
and, for all sufficiently large \(n\), choose \(h_*\in\mathcal H_n\) such that \(r_n\le h_*<2r_n\). Such a grid point exists by \(\mathrm{def:dyadic\text{-}grid}\), because \(r_n\downarrow0\), \(r_n<h_0\) eventually, and \(r_n/(h_0 2^{-\lceil\log_2 n\rceil})\to\infty\).

Let \(\mathcal N_*\) be a maximal \(h_*/2\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\). Compactness of \(\mathcal B\) and maximality make \(\mathcal N_*\) an \(h_*/2\)-net, while the boundary-entropy member property gives
\[
 |\mathcal N_*|\le 2C_{\mathcal B}h_*^{-1}. \tag{104}
\]
For \(z\in\mathcal N_*\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), define the proof-intermediate count
\[
 \widetilde N_{t,n}(z)=\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,z)\le h_*/2\}.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), this is binomial with success probability
\[
 q_{t,P}(z,h_*/2)\ge c_m(h_*/2)^\kappa. \tag{105}
\]
For \(Z\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), Markov's inequality applied to the nonnegative variable \(2^{-Z}\) yields
\[
 \Pr\{Z\le nq/2\}
 \le 2^{nq/2}\mathbb E[2^{-Z}]
 =2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n
 \le \exp\{-nq(1-\log2)/2\}\le e^{-nq/8}. \tag{106}
\]
The equality uses the binomial generating function, and the first exponential inequality uses \(\log(1-u)\le-u\) for \(0\le u<1\).

Take the union bound in (106) over (104) and both sides. If \(x\in\mathcal B\), choose \(z\in\mathcal N_*\) with \(d(x,z)\le h_*/2\); then \(B(z,h_*/2)\subseteq B(x,h_*)\). We therefore obtain an event \(G_n\) and constants \(c,C>0\), depending only on the declared envelopes, such that uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{base}}\),
\[
 \inf_{x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}}N_{t,n}(x,h_*)\ge cnh_*^\kappa,
 \qquad
 P(G_n^c)\le Ch_*^{-1}e^{-cnh_*^\kappa}. \tag{107}
\]
From (103) and \(h_*\asymp r_n\),
\[
 nh_*^{\kappa+2}\asymp\log n,
 \qquad
 \frac{nh_*^\kappa}{\log(e+n/h_*)}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{108}
\]
Equations (107)--(108) show that \(h_*\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\) for every \(x,t\) on \(G_n\), for all sufficiently large \(n\). The minimizing property in \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\), comparison with \(h_*\), (107), and (108) now imply
\[
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/\widehat h_{t,n}(x))}
 {N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))}}\le C r_n \quad\text{on }G_n, \tag{109}
\]
simultaneously in \(x,t\). Indeed, the objective at \(h_*\) is bounded by
\[
 Lh_*+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h_*)}{cnh_*^\kappa}}\le C r_n, \tag{110}
\]
where the last inequality follows from \(h_*\asymp r_n\) and \(nr_n^{\kappa+2}=\log n\).

The elementary bounds \(|\mathcal H_n|\le 2+\log_2 n\) and \(\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\le Cn^3\) give
\[
 \log(2M_n/\gamma)\le C_\gamma\log n
 \le C_\gamma\log(e+n/\widehat h_{t,n}(x)), \tag{111}
\]
because \(0<\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\le h_0<1\). On \(G_n\) the selected count is positive, so (109) and (111) give
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}}B_{t,n}(x)\le C_\gamma r_n. \tag{112}
\]
On \(G_n^c\), the definition of \(B_{t,n}\), \(h_0<1\), and \(N\ge1\) in its positive-count branch give the deterministic bound
\[
 \sup_{x,t}B_{t,n}(x)\le L+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)}. \tag{113}
\]
Furthermore, (103), (107), and \(h_*\asymp r_n\) imply
\[
 h_*^{-1}e^{-cnh_*^\kappa}\sqrt{\log(2M_n/\gamma)}=o(r_n), \tag{114}
\]
because \(nh_*^\kappa\) grows as a positive power of \(n\), up to a logarithmic factor, and hence its exponential dominates every polynomial and logarithm. Since the displayed interval has
\[
 W_n(x)=B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x), \tag{115}
\]
splitting the expectation over \(G_n\) and \(G_n^c\), then applying (107) and (112)--(114), proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)\le
 C_\gamma\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}. \tag{116}
\]

Now suppose \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\), and let a band sequence have simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) on that class, where \(\epsilon_n\downarrow0\). All premises of \(\mathrm{lem:geometry\text{-}general\text{-}pervasive\text{-}band\text{-}width\text{-}obstruction}\) hold: the assignment regions are complementary, the geometry satisfies global boundary entropy, and the class definition supplies the base conditions together with pervasive thin sites. That lemma therefore gives, for every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)\ge
 c_\gamma\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}, \tag{117}
\]
and also
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}}\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 \frac{\mathbb E_PW_n(x)}{r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)}\ge c_\gamma. \tag{118}
\]
These conclusions are geometry-general. The role of \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) is only to exhibit one specification for which the pervasive class is nonempty. Since \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\subseteq\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{base}}\), a band honest over the base class is honest over the pervasive subclass, and its base-class supremum is at least the supremum in (117). Conversely, (116) applies to the displayed band on both the base class and its pervasive subclass. Equations (116)--(117) thus prove its matched global expected-supremum half-width frontier on both classes, while (118) is the asserted local-benchmark converse.

Finally, we prove the two-law inequality independently of pervasive thinning. Fix \(x\in\mathcal B\), and for \(j=0,1\) let
\[
 A_j=\{\tau_{P_j}(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\}.
\]
Simultaneous coverage over a class containing \(P_0,P_1\) implies
\[
 P_j^{\otimes n}(A_j)\ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n,\qquad j=0,1. \tag{119}
\]
By the defining variational inequality for total variation of the full observed product laws,
\[
 P_0^{\otimes n}(A_1)\ge P_1^{\otimes n}(A_1)
 -\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n}). \tag{120}
\]
Combining (119)--(120) with \(P_0(A_0\cap A_1)\ge P_0(A_0)+P_0(A_1)-1\) gives
\[
 P_0^{\otimes n}(A_0\cap A_1)\ge
 1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n}). \tag{121}
\]
On \(A_0\cap A_1\), the interval \(\mathcal C_n(x)\) contains both target values, so its half-diameter satisfies
\[
 W_n(x)\ge\frac12|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|. \tag{122}
\]
Multiplying (122) by the indicator of \(A_0\cap A_1\), taking the \(P_0\)-expectation, and using the positive part of (121) proves
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge
 \frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
This last argument necessarily compares full observed laws. It does not turn score-law total variation into full-law distinguishability, and the global factor in (111) need not match the bounded local multiplicity term in \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}\). Accordingly, the theorem asserts neither local-oracle width achievability over an arbitrary triangular union nor an exact score-law adaptation criterion.
