semantic_closure.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). The estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the score density. Uniformly for \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\right]
 \le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},
 \qquad
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
The fallback event obeys
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 P\{\exists x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}:\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\}
 \le Cn^3\exp\{-c n c_m h_0^{\kappa}\},
\]
and this event's contribution is included in the expected-risk bound.  Consequently, whenever \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\),
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})
 \asymp R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}})
 \asymp (\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
semantic_closure.justification: This gives a single count-qualified estimator uniformly over the maximal polynomial lower-mass class, retains the pervasive packing converse, and closes both base and pervasive minimax frontiers when the pervasive subclass is nonempty.
semantic_closure.gap: Positive-density and finitely-degenerate univariate sup-norm results do not provide a two-sided vanishing-mass boundary estimator uniform over this base class or the same-modulus pervasive converse.
semantic_closure.consumer: The \(R\), Python, and Stata \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflows can use observed-count bandwidths throughout the base class without knowing \(\kappa\), with a specified safe fallback.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
The complementary assignment regions and the definition of \(T\) imply \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\) if and only if \(T_i=t\). The definitions of the empirical counts, local-constant fits, admissible sets, deterministic tie break, and fallback show that \(\widehat\tau_n\) is a single measurable map of \(\mathcal D_n\), the known geometry, \(L\), \(\sigma\), and \(n\). In particular, it uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the score density.

Fix \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\), let \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\), and put
\[
 r=(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the dyadic grid in \(\mathrm{def:dyadic\text{-}grid}\) contains \(h_*\) satisfying \(r\le h_*<2r\). Let \(z_1,\ldots,z_J\) be a maximal \(h_*/2\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\). Maximality makes it an \(h_*/2\)-net, and the upper half of \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\), inherited through \(\mathrm{def:base\text{-}thickness\text{-}class}\), gives
\[
 J\le 2C_{\mathcal B}h_*^{-1}. \tag{35}
\]
For every net center and side, the polynomial lower-mass member property gives
\[
 q_{t,P}(z_j,h_*/2)\ge c_m(h_*/2)^\kappa. \tag{36}
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), the associated count is binomial. If \(N\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), Markov's inequality applied to \(2^{-N}\) yields
\[
 \Pr\{N\le nq/2\}
 \le 2^{nq/2}\mathbb E(2^{-N})
 =2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n
 \le e^{-nq/8}. \tag{37}
\]
Taking a union bound over (35), the two sides, and (36), and then using \(B(z_j,h_*/2)\subseteq B(x,h_*)\) whenever \(d(x,z_j)\le h_*/2\), produces a score-measurable event \(G_n\) on which
\[
 \inf_{x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}}N_{t,n}(x,h_*)
 \ge c n c_mh_*^\kappa, \tag{38}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}P(G_n^c)
 \le Ch_*^{-1}\exp\{-c n c_mh_*^\kappa\}. \tag{39}
\]
Because \(h_*\asymp r\),
\[
 \frac{nh_*^\kappa}{\log(e+n/h_*)}
 \ge c\left(\frac n{\log n}\right)^{2/(\overline\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty \tag{40}
\]
uniformly over the declared exponent range. Hence (38) makes \(h_*\) admissible for every \(x,t\) on \(G_n\), for all sufficiently large \(n\). The minimizing property in \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\), (38), and \(nr^{\kappa+2}=\log n\) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)
 +\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/\widehat h_{t,n}(x))}
 {N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))}}\\
 &\qquad\le Lh_*+
 \sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h_*)}{c n c_mh_*^\kappa}}
 \le Cr.
 \end{aligned} \tag{41}
\]

The lower-mass condition also supplies the support premise needed at the boundary. For any \(x\in\mathcal B\), side \(t\), and radius \(s>0\), taking \(b=\min\{h_0,s/2\}\) gives
\[
 P_X\{X\in\mathcal A_t:d(X,x)<s\}
 \ge q_{t,P}(x,b)\ge c_mb^\kappa>0. \tag{42}
\]
Thus \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\). The Lipschitz member property and the trace definition yield
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x). \tag{43}
\]
For a nonempty selected averaging set, every included score lies within \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) of \(x\), so (43) bounds its conditional bias by \(L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\).

Let \(Z_n\) be the maximum of the normalized residual sums over the nonempty disk patterns in \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\). That lemma, which was proved above from the corrected observed-side kernel condition, and \(|\mathcal H_n|\le 2+\log_2 n\) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P(Z_n\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)\le C\sqrt{\log n}. \tag{44}
\]
Because \(h\le h_0<1\) entails \(\log(e+n/h)\ge\log n\), equations (41), (43), and (44), followed by the triangle inequality over the two sides, give
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]\mathbf 1_{G_n}
 \le Cr\mathbf 1_{G_n}. \tag{45}
\]

On \(G_n^c\), a selected set is either nonempty or is the \(h_0\)-fallback. If it is nonempty, (43), Lipschitzness, and \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\le h_0\) bound its conditional mean error by \(Lh_0\); if it is empty, the fit is zero and the bounded-trace member property bounds the trace error by \(L\). Since every nonempty count is at least one, (44) therefore gives the conditional bound \(C\{L+\sigma\sqrt{\log n}\}\) for the supremum loss. The right-hand side of (39) decreases faster than any power uniformly in \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\), by (40). Integrating (45) and the off-event bound proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le Cr. \tag{46}
\]

For the fallback probability, repeat the net argument with the fixed radius \(h_0/2\). The net has at most \(2C_{\mathcal B}h_0^{-1}\) points, while every center-side count has expectation at least \(nc_m(h_0/2)^\kappa\), which uniformly exceeds \(16\log(e+n/h_0)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Equation (37), a union bound, and ball inclusion imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 P\{\exists x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}:\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\}
 \le C\exp\{-c n c_mh_0^\kappa\}
 \le Cn^3\exp\{-c n c_mh_0^\kappa\}. \tag{47}
\]
The off-event calculation above already includes this event's contribution.

Finally, \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) by \(\mathrm{def:pervasive\text{-}thinning\text{-}class}\). The single-estimator bound (46) gives both \(R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}})\le Cr\) and \(R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\le Cr\). The pervasive converse in \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), certified by \(\mathrm{lem:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}validity}\) and \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), gives \(R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge cr\). When the pervasive subclass is nonempty, monotonicity of minimax risk under class inclusion gives
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}})
 \ge R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge cr. \tag{48}
\]
Equations (46)--(48) establish both matched frontiers.

semantic_closure.statement:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the residual \(\varepsilon_t=Y-g_{t,P}(X)\) is conditionally integrable and satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_P[\exp(\lambda\varepsilon_t)\mid X=z]\le \exp(\sigma^2\lambda^2/2)\quad\text{for every }\lambda\in\mathbb R,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[|\varepsilon_t|\mid X=z]\le \sigma\sqrt{2\pi}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]=g_{t,P}(z)\) at every such \(z\).

Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},
 \qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le 2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and the centered score-conditional sub-Gaussian kernel condition \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), adopt the convention that the maximum below is zero when \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\). For \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-almost every score vector, conditionally on the scores and with \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), one has for every \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le 2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
The conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most
\[
 \sqrt{2\log\{2(1\vee|\mathscr S_n|)\}}+1.
\]
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix a score vector outside the \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-null set on which either a conditional-kernel assertion or the conditional product factorization below fails.

For the deterministic trace count, membership of a fixed point \(X_i\) in a closed disk with center \(c\in\mathbb R^2\) and radius \(r\) is equivalent to
\[
 2c^{\mathsf T}X_i+s\ge \lVert X_i\rVert_2^2,
 \qquad s=r^2-\lVert c\rVert_2^2. \tag{11}
\]
Thus every disk trace on \(\{X_1,\ldots,X_n\}\) is a sign pattern induced by \(n\) affine hyperplanes in the three-dimensional parameter \((c_1,c_2,s)\). Any trace realized by a closed disk can be made strict without changing the trace: if a point is excluded, its distance from the closed disk is positive and the radius may be increased by less than the minimum of these finitely many positive distances; if no point is excluded, any sufficiently small increase works. Hence equality in (11) creates no additional trace.

Let \(A(n,v)\) be the largest number of open cells cut out by \(n\) affine hyperplanes in \(\mathbb R^v\). Adding the last hyperplane retains the old cells and splits at most \(A(n-1,v-1)\) of them, because the induced arrangement on that hyperplane has dimension \(v-1\). Therefore
\[
 A(n,v)\le A(n-1,v)+A(n-1,v-1),
 \qquad A(0,v)=A(n,0)=1. \tag{12}
\]
Induction and Pascal's identity yield
\[
 A(n,3)\le\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj. \tag{13}
\]
Restricting to genuine disks of a fixed radius, restricting their centers to \(\mathcal B\), and intersecting a trace with the fixed side set \(\{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t\}\) cannot increase the number of traces. There are two sides and \(|\mathcal H_n|\) radii by \(\mathrm{def:dyadic\text{-}grid}\), so
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj. \tag{14}
\]

If \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\), both stochastic conclusions follow from the stipulated zero-maximum convention. Suppose otherwise. By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), regular conditional laws of the observations given \((X_1,\ldots,X_n)\) factor for \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-almost every score vector; consequently the residuals are conditionally independent. The definition \(T=\mathbf 1\{X\in\mathcal A_1\}\) and the partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) give \(T_i=t\) for every index in a side-\(t\) candidate set. Moreover, the restricted score measure gives full mass to its closed support \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\): its complement is a countable union of rational basic open sets of restricted mass zero. After removing the two null sets declared in \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), that assumption therefore gives, for every relevant index and every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P\{e^{\lambda\varepsilon_i}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\}
 &=\int_{\mathbb R}
 e^{\lambda\{y-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\}}\,\mathsf R_P(X_i,dy)\\
 &\le e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{15}
\]
The same assumption supplies conditional integrability and zero conditional mean. This is precisely the corrected single-kernel, restricted-measure formulation; no Gaussian equality is used.

For nonempty \(S\in\mathscr S_n\), put
\[
 Z_S=\frac1{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i.
\]
Conditional independence and (15) imply, for every \(u\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\{e^{uZ_S}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\}
 \le\prod_{i\in S}e^{u^2/(2|S|)}=e^{u^2/2}. \tag{16}
\]
Markov's inequality applied to \(e^{zZ_S}\) and then to \(e^{-zZ_S}\) gives
\[
 \Pr_P\{|Z_S|>z\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\}\le2e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
A union bound over \(S\), which requires no independence among the set-indexed sums, proves
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}|Z_S|>z
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}. \tag{17}
\]

Finally let \(z_0=\sqrt{2\log\{2|\mathscr S_n|\}}\). Since \(|\mathscr S_n|\ge1\), one has \(z_0>1\). The tail-integral identity for nonnegative random variables, (17), and
\[
 \int_{z_0}^{\infty}e^{-z^2/2}\,dz\le z_0^{-1}e^{-z_0^2/2}
\]
give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P\left[\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}|Z_S|
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 &\le z_0+2|\mathscr S_n|\int_{z_0}^{\infty}e^{-z^2/2}\,dz\\
 &\le z_0+z_0^{-1}\le z_0+1.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Together with the empty-family case, this is the claimed expectation bound with \(1\vee|\mathscr S_n|\).

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), use the circular inside--outside assignment and constants certified by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), and suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\).  Put \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare
\[
 \mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=\mathbf 1\{u\ge C_mh^\kappa\},
 \qquad 0<h\le h_0,\quad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\cup
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}),
\]
and there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \le R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \le C\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 {r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The displayed inclusion and matched rate expose an internal limitation of the frozen arbitrary-modulus OEQ's lower-profile-only exact-characterization demand for the two-argument class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\): matching same-class bounds cannot recover the isolated polynomial frontier when \(\mathsf J_{-}\) declares one thin site, because the class still retains the pervasive subclass. This is a limitation of that class parameterization, not a refutation of any published estimator or workflow. An arbitrary-modulus formulation that separates isolated from pervasive thinning must add an upper thin-site packing restriction or use an intrinsic two-sided profile.
semantic_closure.justification: This theorem gives an explicit same-class polynomial witness for which a constant declared lower packing profile nevertheless has the pervasive logarithmic minimax rate.
semantic_closure.gap: An exact arbitrary-modulus frontier for a refined class with upper as well as lower thin-site packing control remains unresolved; the frozen two-argument class cannot express the isolated side of that comparison.
semantic_closure.consumer: The \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflow must not interpret a constant lower packing declaration as evidence of isolated thinning; it needs an upper-profile certificate before using an isolated-rate guarantee.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
All statements below concern the independent product experiment in \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\). First, the displayed declarations are well typed. Since \(\kappa>2\) and \(c_m>0\), the map \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) is positive and nondecreasing on \((0,h_0]\). The constants certified by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) admit a circular member satisfying \(c_mh^\kappa\le q_{t,P}(x,h)\le1\) at every admissible radius, so \(m(h)\in(0,1]\). The declared map \(\mathsf J_{-}\) takes values in \(\mathbb N_0\) and is nondecreasing in its second argument.

We next prove the two class inclusions. Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso}}\). By \(\mathrm{def:isolated\text{-}thinning\text{-}class}\) and \(\mathrm{def:base\text{-}thickness\text{-}class}\), \(P\) has all sharp-assignment, consistency, boundary-entropy, Lipschitz, bounded-trace, and corrected observed-side conditional sub-Gaussian properties required by \(\mathrm{def:modulus\text{-}profile\text{-}class}\). Its polynomial lower-mass property gives, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\),
\[
 q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge c_mh^\kappa=m(h). \tag{66}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:minimum\text{-}side\text{-}mass}\) and the definition of \(\mathsf J_P\), if \(u\le u'\), then
\[
 \{x\in\mathcal B:a_P(x,h)\le u\}
 \subseteq
 \{x\in\mathcal B:a_P(x,h)\le u'\},
 \qquad
 \mathsf J_P(h,u)\le\mathsf J_P(h,u'). \tag{67}
\]
If \(u<C_mh^\kappa\), then \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=0\le\mathsf J_P(h,u)\). If \(u\ge C_mh^\kappa\), equation (67) and \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}site}\) give
\[
 \mathsf J_P(h,u)
 \ge\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^\kappa)
 \ge1
 =\mathsf J_{-}(h,u). \tag{68}
\]
Equations (66)--(68), together with \(\mathrm{def:modulus\text{-}profile\text{-}class}\), prove \(P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\).

Now fix \(P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\). The same base-class argument proves (66). If \(u\ge C_mh^\kappa\), equation (67) and \(\mathrm{ass:pervasive\text{-}thin\text{-}sites}\) give
\[
 \mathsf J_P(h,u)
 \ge\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^\kappa)
 \ge c_Jh^{-1}>0.
\]
Because \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\in\mathbb N_0\), strict positivity implies \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\ge1=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\); below the threshold the declared lower profile is zero. Hence
\[
 \mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso}}\cup
 \mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \subseteq\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}). \tag{69}
\]
The circular membership lemma supplies a member of each subclass, so all classes used below are nonempty.

For law classes \(\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathcal P\), \(\mathrm{def:expected\text{-}sup\text{-}risk}\) gives, for every estimator \(\widetilde\tau_n\) measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\) and the known assignment geometry,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 |\widetilde\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \ge
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 |\widetilde\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|.
\]
Taking the infimum over the identical estimator set on both sides proves
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P)\ge R_n(\mathcal Q). \tag{70}
\]
Apply (70) to the pervasive inclusion in (69), and then apply the pervasive lower bound from \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\). Its nonemptiness and circular-geometry premises are supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), and its partition premise is the assumed equality \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Thus there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \ge R_n(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}})
 \ge c\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}. \tag{71}
\]

For the reverse inequality, set
\[
 s_n=\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
Then \(s_n\downarrow0\), \(ns_n\to\infty\), and, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the grid in \(\mathrm{def:dyadic\text{-}grid}\) contains a point \(h_n\) such that
\[
 s_n\le h_n<2s_n,
 \qquad h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n. \tag{72}
\]
Indeed, take the numerically smallest grid point no smaller than \(s_n\). Since \(h_0/n<s_n<h_0/2\) eventually, this point is neither endpoint of the grid, and its dyadic predecessor is \(2h_n\). From (72), \(m(h_n)=c_mh_n^\kappa\), and \(\log(e+n/h_n)\le C_0\log n\) for a fixed \(C_0<\infty\) eventually, we obtain
\[
 \frac{nm(h_n)}{\log(e+n/h_n)}
 \ge\frac{c_mns_n^\kappa}{C_0\log n}
 =\frac{c_m}{C_0}
 \left(\frac n{\log n}\right)^{2/(\kappa+2)}
 \longrightarrow\infty. \tag{73}
\]
Thus (73) eventually implies the count qualification in \(\mathrm{thm:arbitrary\text{-}modulus\text{-}two\text{-}sided\text{-}bracket}\). Evaluate that theorem's explicit clipped count-adaptive estimator at the feasible bandwidth \(h_n\). Equations (72)--(73) imply constants \(C_1,C_2,C_3<\infty\), independent of \(n\), for which
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 |\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\\
 &\quad\le C_1\left\{Lh_n+
 \sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h_n)}{nm(h_n)}}\right\}\\
 &\quad\le C_2\left\{s_n+
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{ns_n^\kappa}}\right\}
 =C_3s_n,
 \end{aligned} \tag{74}
\]
where the last equality uses \(s_n^{\kappa+2}=\log n/n\). This clipped count-adaptive estimator is a single estimator measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\) and the known assignment geometry, and it does not depend on the member law \(P\). It is therefore an admissible competitor in \(\mathrm{def:expected\text{-}sup\text{-}risk}\), so (74) gives
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \le C_3s_n
 =C_3r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}. \tag{75}
\]
Combining (71) and (75) proves the asserted matched pervasive rate on the lower-profile-only class.

Finally,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =\frac{(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}}{n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{76}
\]
If the one-site lower declaration recovered the isolated frontier, the risk would be bounded above by a constant multiple of \(r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\), contradicting (71) and (76). The generic-class certificate is the entire pervasive circular subclass retained by (69), not merely a single law. Hence a class constrained only by the scalar lower-mass modulus and a lower packing declaration cannot distinguish isolated from pervasive thinning. An upper thin-site packing restriction or an intrinsic two-sided profile is required for a formulation that separates the two regimes.

semantic_closure.condition: \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge m(h)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\).

novel.justification: A declared common modulus records the weakest two-sided local information available along the boundary and can be estimated from score-only pilot data in geographic designs.

novel.justification: A lower packing envelope describes guaranteed multiplicity of sparse boundary segments and is directly realized by repeated tubular depletion.

semantic_closure.statement:
Let \(M\ge2\), let \(Q_0,\ldots,Q_M\) be probability laws on a common measurable space, and suppose \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)<\infty\) for every \(j\). For every decoder \(\widehat J\) taking values in \(\{0,\ldots,M\}\),
\[
 \frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M Q_j\{\widehat J\ne j\}
 \ge
 \frac{\log(M+1)-\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)-\log2}{\log M}.
\]
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Let \(J\) be uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,M\}\), and, conditionally on \(J=j\), let the observation \(Z\) have law \(Q_j\). Put \(\overline Q=(M+1)^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^M Q_j\) and
\[
 p_e=\Pr\{\widehat J(Z)\ne J\}.
\]
Since every \(Q_j\) is absolutely continuous with respect to \(Q_0\), all laws are dominated by \(Q_0\). Direct expansion of the logarithms gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)
 &=\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,\overline Q)
   +\operatorname{KL}(\overline Q,Q_0)\\
 &\ge \frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,\overline Q)
 =I(J;Z),
 \end{aligned} \tag{1}
\]
where the inequality is the nonnegativity of relative entropy, obtained from \(u\log u-u+1\ge0\) after integration. Let \(E=\mathbf 1\{\widehat J(Z)\ne J\}\). Because \(E\) is determined by \((J,Z)\), the entropy chain rule gives
\[
 H(J\mid Z)=H(E\mid Z)+H(J\mid E,Z).
\]
The binary entropy is at most \(\log2\). Conditional on \(E=0\), the value of \(J\) is determined by \(Z\); conditional on \(E=1\) and \(Z\), at most \(M\) values remain possible. The entropy of a distribution on at most \(k\) points is at most \(\log k\), by concavity of \(-u\log u\). Consequently,
\[
 H(J\mid Z)\le\log2+p_e\log M. \tag{2}
\]
On the other hand, uniformity of \(J\) and the definition of mutual information imply
\[
 H(J\mid Z)=\log(M+1)-I(J;Z). \tag{3}
\]
Combining (1)--(3), rearranging, and observing that \(\log M>0\) proves the displayed inequality. Finally, the definition of the joint experiment gives
\[
 p_e=\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M Q_j\{\widehat J\ne j\},
\]
which completes the proof.

semantic_closure.statement: Let \(Q_0,\ldots,Q_M\) be probability laws and let \(v_0,\ldots,v_M\) be elements of a metric space whose metric \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}\) satisfies \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(v_j,v_k)\ge 2\delta\) for \(j\ne k\). If \(M\ge2\) and \(M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)\le a\log M\), where \(0<a<1/8\), then every estimator \(\widehat v\) satisfies \(\max_{0\le j\le M}\mathbb E_{Q_j}\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_j)\ge c\delta\) for a numerical \(c>0\). If \(M=1\) and \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)\le1/8\), the same conclusion holds. These conclusions also hold for product experiments after replacing each \(Q_j\) by its product law.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
For the two-law assertion, let an estimator induce a nearest-point test \(\widehat J\in\{0,1\}\). On \(\{\widehat J\ne j\}\), the triangle inequality and \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(v_0,v_1)\ge2\delta\) imply \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_j)\ge\delta\). The smallest average testing error is
\[
 \frac12\int \min(dQ_0,dQ_1)=\frac{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)}2. \tag{11}
\]
For every measurable event \(A\), the log-sum inequality for the partition \(\{A,A^c\}\) gives, with \(p=Q_1(A)\) and \(q=Q_0(A)\),
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)
 \ge p\log\frac pq+(1-p)\log\frac{1-p}{1-q}
 \ge2(p-q)^2. \tag{12}
\]
The last inequality follows by integrating the second derivative \(1/\{p(1-p)\}\ge4\) of the binary relative entropy as a function of \(p\), whose value and first derivative vanish at \(p=q\). Taking the supremum over \(A\) in (12) yields
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\le\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)/2}\le1/4.
\]
Equation (11) and the nearest-point implication therefore make the maximum risk at least \(3\delta/8\).

For \(M\ge2\), let \(J\) be uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,M\}\), draw \(Z\) from \(Q_J\), and put \(\overline Q=(M+1)^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^M Q_j\). Expansion of the logarithms gives, for any dominating law \(Q\),
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q)
 =\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,\overline Q)
 +(M+1)\operatorname{KL}(\overline Q,Q). \tag{13}
\]
Taking \(Q=Q_0\) in (13) bounds the mutual information by
\[
 I(J;Z)=\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,\overline Q)
 \le\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=1}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)
 \le a\log M. \tag{14}
\]
For any decoder, if \(p_e=\Pr(\widehat J\ne J)\), conditioning entropy first on the error indicator and then, on error, on at most \(M\) alternatives gives
\[
 H(J\mid Z)\le\log2+p_e\log M.
\]
Since \(H(J)=\log(M+1)\) and \(I(J;Z)=H(J)-H(J\mid Z)\), (14) implies
\[
 p_e\ge
 \frac{\log(M+1)-a\log M-\log2}{\log M}. \tag{15}
\]
For \(M\ge2\) and \(0<a<1/8\), the right side has a positive numerical lower bound. Nearest-point decoding again implies \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_J)\ge\delta\) on error. Averaging over \(J\), then bounding the average risk by the maximum risk, proves the stated conclusion. The argument concerns only the supplied laws, so replacing each by its product experiment leaves it unchanged.

semantic_closure.statement: Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), an assignment geometry satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) and \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), and constants for which \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) are nonempty; \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) supplies an explicit such specification. The two classes share the scalar lower modulus \(c_mh^{\kappa}\), but there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). Thus no expected-sup minimax frontier is a functional of the common scalar modulus alone, and the frontier separates according to the declared thin-site multiplicity profile.
semantic_closure.justification: The theorem identifies multiplicity of thin locations, rather than local mass at the single worst point, as the missing information coordinate for uniform boundary estimation.
semantic_closure.gap: Gaiffas2007SharpSupNorm gives an unknown-density, spatially normalized univariate sup-norm estimator under a positive continuous design density, Gaiffas2009Uniform treats finitely many univariate density zeros, and AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 studies known-design global \(L^2\) loss; none gives a same-modulus isolated-versus-pervasive expected-sup separation for a two-sided causal boundary.
semantic_closure.consumer: Users of the full boundary causal trace curve can distinguish one local data desert from boundary-wide depletion before interpreting a worst-case uniform rate.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
For a law \(P\), define the finite one-sided score measure \(\mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t)\). If \(P\) is in either stated class, \(x\in\mathcal B\), and \(r>0\), set \(s=\min\{h_0,r/2\}\). The polynomial lower-mass member property gives
\[
 \mu_{t,P}\{z:d(z,x)<r\}\ge q_{t,P}(x,s)\ge c_ms^\kappa>0. \tag{18}
\]
Thus every boundary point lies in \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\). Lipschitz continuity of the distinguished regression representative and the definition of the trace imply
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x),\qquad t\in\{0,1\},\ x\in\mathcal B. \tag{19}
\]
The partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and the definition of \(T\) make \(X\in\mathcal A_t\) equivalent to \(T=t\), so the side averages used below estimate the observed-law functional in (19). Consistency, which is a member property of both classes, supplies its causal interpretation as \(\tau_P\).

We first prove the lower bounds by experiments lying in the very classes over which risk is taken. Start from any member of the nonempty class at issue, retain its score law and geometry, take independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), and set \(Y(s)=\sigma Z_s\). Call the resulting law \(Q_0\). It remains in the same class: every design condition is unchanged, the side regressions and traces are zero, and the single observed-outcome kernel is \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\), which satisfies each restricted-side integrability, centering, and MGF clause in \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\).

For the isolated class set \(h=a_0n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\). For large \(n\), \(h\le h_0/3\). The isolated thin-site property supplies \(x_h\in\mathcal B\) and \(t_h\in\{0,1\}\) such that
\[
 q_{t_h,Q_0}(x_h,h)=a_{Q_0}(x_h,h)\le C_mh^\kappa. \tag{20}
\]
Let \(\psi_h(z)=(1-3d(z,x_h)/h)_+\) and \(\eta_h=Lh/12\). If \(t_h=1\), add \(\eta_h\psi_h(X)\) to \(Y(1)\); if \(t_h=0\), subtract it from \(Y(0)\); leave the other potential outcome unchanged. Since \(\eta_h\psi_h\) is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz, is bounded by \(L\), and changes neither the score law nor the centered Gaussian observed residual kernel, the resulting law \(Q_1\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso}}\). By (19),
\[
 \|\tau_{Q_1}-\tau_{Q_0}\|_\infty\ge\eta_h. \tag{21}
\]
Direct Gaussian likelihood-ratio integration and (20) give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =\frac{n\eta_h^2}{2\sigma^2}\int\psi_h(z)^2\,d\mu_{t_h,Q_0}(z)
 \le \frac{nC_mL^2h^{\kappa+2}}{288\sigma^2}. \tag{22}
\]
Choose \(a_0>0\) so the last expression is at most \(1/8\). The two-law clause of \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), with supremum distance and \(2\delta=\eta_h\), yields
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso}})\ge c n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}=c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}. \tag{23}
\]

For the pervasive class set \(h=a_0(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\). Its thin-site property supplies an \(h\)-separated set \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) with
\[
 M\ge c_Jh^{-1},\qquad a_{Q_0}(x_j,h)\le C_mh^\kappa. \tag{24}
\]
At each \(x_j\), choose a side attaining the minimum and perturb that side by a radius-\(h/3\), height-\(Lh/12\) tent, with the sign chosen to increase the contrast. Exactly as above, the resulting \(Q_j\) lie in \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\). Their target curves are pairwise separated by at least \(Lh/12\), because every other tent vanishes at \(x_j\). The calculation in (22) gives
\[
 \max_{1\le j\le M}\operatorname{KL}(Q_j^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le Cnh^{\kappa+2}=Ca_0^{\kappa+2}\log n. \tag{25}
\]
Equation (24) implies \(\log M\ge c_\kappa\log n\) eventually. Taking \(a_0\) sufficiently small makes (25) at most \(a\log M\), where \(a<1/8\) is the constant in \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\). Its multiple-law clause yields
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge c(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}=c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}. \tag{26}
\]
The exact centered-Gaussian circular experiments of \(\mathrm{lem:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}validity}\) give explicit witnesses to the same information budgets.

For the upper bounds, let \(s_n\) denote the rate claimed for the class at issue. Choose \(b\in\mathcal H_n\) so that, for all large \(n\),
\[
 s_n\le b<2s_n,\qquad b/2\in\mathcal H_n,\qquad b\le h_0/2. \tag{27}
\]
Take a deterministic maximal \(b/2\)-separated boundary net \(z_1,\ldots,z_M\). Global boundary entropy gives \(M\le2C_{\mathcal B}b^{-1}\). Let \(j(x)\) be the least net index within \(b/2\) of \(x\), define the radius-\(b\) side counts \(K_{t,j}\) and means \(\bar g_{t,j}\), and use the single data-driven estimator
\[
 \widetilde\tau_{n,b}(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\bar g_{1,j(x)}-\bar g_{0,j(x)}\}. \tag{28}
\]
It is measurable in the sample and known geometry. Projection cannot increase the error because \(|\tau_P(x)|\le2L\). On \(K_{t,j(x)}>0\), every included score lies within \(3b/2\) of \(x\), so (19) and Lipschitz smoothness give conditional bias at most \(3Lb/2\).

If \(N\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), Markov's inequality applied to \(2^{-N}\) and \(1-y\le e^{-y}\) give
\[
 \Pr(N\le nq/2)\le2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n\le e^{-nq/8}. \tag{29}
\]
For the pervasive rate, polynomial lower mass, (29), and a union bound over the net and two sides give an event \(H_b\) on which all \(K_{t,j}\ge nc_mb^\kappa/2\) and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}}P(H_b^c)
 \le Cb^{-1}e^{-cnb^\kappa}. \tag{30}
\]
Conditional on the scores, independent sampling factorizes the single observed-outcome kernels, and the corrected restricted-side MGF clauses apply at every selected score. Hence \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\) gives conditional expected maximum normalized residual sum at most \(C\sqrt{\log(en)}\). Therefore, on \(H_b\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \max_{t,j}|\bar g_{t,j}-\mathbb E_P(\bar g_{t,j}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)|
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 \le C\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(en)}{nc_mb^\kappa}}\le C_\kappa b, \tag{31}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(nb^{\kappa+2}\asymp\log n\). The clipped loss is at most \(4L\) on \(H_b^c\); equations (30)--(31) and the bias bound prove the pervasive upper rate.

For the isolated rate, \(nb^\kappa\asymp b^{-2}\). Fix a side, take \(D\ge C_m\), put \(u_\ell=\min\{1,D2^\ell b^\kappa\}\), and group net centers by \(q_{t,P}(z_j,b)\le u_0\) or \(u_{\ell-1}<q_{t,P}(z_j,b)\le u_\ell\). Such centers obey \(a_P(z_j,b/2)\le u_\ell\). They are \(b/2\)-separated, so the isolated upper profile gives
\[
 M_\ell\le C_\kappa\{1+2^{\ell/(\kappa-2)}\}. \tag{32}
\]
In group zero the mean count is at least \(cb^{-2}\), and in group \(\ell\ge1\) it is at least \(c2^\ell b^{-2}\). Summing (29) with (32) over groups and sides produces an event \(H_b\) on which every group-\(\ell\) count is at least \(c2^\ell b^{-2}\) and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso}}}P(H_b^c)
 \le C_\kappa\sum_{\ell\ge0}\{1+2^{\ell/(\kappa-2)}\}e^{-c2^\ell/b^2}
 \le C_\kappa e^{-c_\kappa/b^2}. \tag{33}
\]
The same conditional MGF factorization gives, for \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr_P\!\left\{
 \max_{t,j}|\bar g_{t,j}-\mathbb E_P(\bar g_{t,j}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)|>zb
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le C_\kappa\sum_{\ell\ge0}\{1+2^{\ell/(\kappa-2)}\}e^{-cz^22^\ell}. \tag{34}
\]
For all sufficiently large fixed \(z\), the series is at most \(C_\kappa e^{-c_\kappa z^2}\). Integrating this tail shows that the conditional expected stochastic maximum on \(H_b\) is at most \(C_\kappa b\). The bias bound, (33), and the \(4L\) clipped-loss bound off \(H_b\) prove the isolated upper rate.

Thus the estimator (28) witnesses both minimax upper bounds, while (23) and (26) prove the matching lower bounds. Finally,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The common scalar lower modulus therefore cannot determine expected-sup risk; the declared thin-site multiplicity separates the two frontiers.

semantic_closure.statement: For every fixed \(\alpha>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)>0\) for all \(h>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)\asymp h^{\alpha+1}\exp(-h^{-\alpha})\) as \(h\downarrow0\), and there exists \(h_n\downarrow0\) such that \(n m_{\alpha}(h_n)/\log n\to\infty\). Therefore a fixed exponential horn is compatible with logarithmically slow consistency and does not by itself force order-one risk.
semantic_closure.justification: This proposition removes a false early-kill premise before it contaminates the minimax theorem or the applied interpretation.
semantic_closure.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate obtains a logarithmic pointwise rate under severe design degeneracy; the present proposition records the corresponding boundary-modulus sanity condition without claiming a new minimax theorem.
semantic_closure.consumer: Applied analysts will not mistake an extremely thin but positive region for a formally non-estimable boundary segment.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Positivity follows from the strictly positive integrand in \(\mathrm{def:exponential\text{-}modulus}\). With the substitution \(s=u^{-\alpha}\),
\[
 m_\alpha(h)=\frac2\alpha\int_{h^{-\alpha}}^\infty e^{-s}s^{-1/\alpha-1}\,ds.
\]
Let \(a=1+1/\alpha\) and \(x=h^{-\alpha}\). Integration by parts gives
\[
 \int_x^\infty e^{-s}s^{-a}\,ds
 =e^{-x}x^{-a}-a\int_x^\infty e^{-s}s^{-a-1}\,ds.
\]
The last integral is between zero and \(x^{-1}\int_x^\infty e^{-s}s^{-a}\,ds\). Hence the ratio of the first integral to \(e^{-x}x^{-a}\) lies between \((1+a/x)^{-1}\) and one and tends to one. Therefore
\[
 m_\alpha(h)\sim\frac2\alpha h^{\alpha+1}e^{-h^{-\alpha}}
 \qquad(h\downarrow0).
\]
This proves the asserted two-sided asymptotic order.

For all sufficiently large \(n\), choose
\[
 h_n=\left(\tfrac12\log n\right)^{-1/\alpha}.
\]
Then \(h_n\downarrow0\), \(e^{-h_n^{-\alpha}}=n^{-1/2}\), and the preceding equivalence gives
\[
 \frac{n m_\alpha(h_n)}{\log n}
 \asymp n^{1/2}(\log n)^{-(\alpha+1)/\alpha-1}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Thus a fixed positive exponential modulus admits a vanishing bandwidth with diverging effective sample size and does not by itself force order-one risk.

payload.proof_tex:
Fix \(t\in\{0,1\}\). By \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), there are a regular conditional law \(\mathsf R_P(z,dy)\) of \(Y\) given \(X=z\) and a \(\mu_{t,P}\)-null set \(N_{t,P}\) such that the three asserted integral conditions hold at every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus N_{t,P}\). Fix such a \(z\), and set
\[
 Z_z(y)=y-g_{t,P}(z).
\]
The first integral condition in the assumption gives \(\int |Z_z(y)|\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)<\infty\), so the residual is conditionally integrable. The second condition gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]
 =\int Z_z(y)\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)=0,
\]
and the third gives, for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\exp(\lambda\varepsilon_t)\mid X=z]
 =\int e^{\lambda Z_z(y)}\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)
 \le e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}.
\]

It remains to derive the absolute-moment constant. For \(u>0\) and \(\lambda>0\), positivity of the exponential and its lower bound on \(\{Z_z\ge u\}\) imply
\[
 e^{\lambda u}\mathsf R_P(z,\{Z_z\ge u\})
 \le \int_{\{Z_z\ge u\}}e^{\lambda Z_z(y)}\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)
 \le e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}.
\]
Because \(\sigma>0\), choosing \(\lambda=u/\sigma^2\) yields
\[
 \mathsf R_P(z,\{Z_z\ge u\})\le e^{-u^2/(2\sigma^2)}.
\]
Applying the same calculation to \(-Z_z\), using the moment bound at \(-\lambda\), gives
\[
 \mathsf R_P(z,\{Z_z\le-u\})\le e^{-u^2/(2\sigma^2)}.
\]
The pointwise identity \(|Z_z|=\int_0^\infty\mathbf 1\{|Z_z|>u\}\,du\), followed by interchange of the two nonnegative integrals, therefore gives
\[
